  custom timing harness. Taken off: a latency harness written by the builder;
  general metrics, tracing infrastructure and an admin console remain excluded.

- **2026-09-23 — Quarry states intent moves onto the doing-list** (Charlie:

Unblocks the online-only brief's invitation, webhook and scheduled journeys without a second application server: work records whose authority is bound at admission, ids bound to their operation and arguments, declared action results, a generated handler context with a durable record per external step, declared routes and webhooks, scheduled actions under service seats, and `serve` supervising the runtime. Taken off in the same change: "A jobs framework" narrows — actions, effects and scheduled actions get per-operation retries, deadlines and cancellation; priorities, worker pools and dead letters stay out — and the actions card's "supervise the worker as an ordinary Node process" leaves. Stands: no JavaScript in the data plane, no identity provider in the engine, and no `ctx.sql`, projections or SQL reads in this increment.

- **2026-09-15 — the Postgres access boundary moves onto the doing-list** (LLP 3000.009 §10.2, increment C1). Unblocks measuring Postgres behind a batched access boundary instead of row-at-a-time calls: transaction-scoped prefetch, a pipelined commit tail, one portable index-key bound checked on both stores, and the corpus, conformance and device suites on both stores. Taken off in the same change: the evaluation prototype's single-adapter framing, in which the only next step was an unbatched store. Stands: Postgres is not a hosted or deployable target; its refusals of assets, jobs, actions and schedules, and `serve`, `deploy` and backup on Postgres, wait for increment C3.

- **2026-09-13 — word search, effects, service seats and presence move onto the doing-list** (author: "add all the things we need for Clique and Interview"; the full-brief Clique record's remaining capability lines and Interview's adapter responsibilities). What it unblocks: Clique M5's three search scopes online and offline on one index, M6's push seam without connection leases hand-built in tables, M8's digest emitted rather than logged into a table, Interview's phone sign-in and model workers as a service that mints sessions instead of proxying every request, and the ranked feed of LLP 3000.004 on the `feeds` card. Taken off in the same change: "an embedded JS engine for effects, until measured" (the engine never calls out; a worker does), "word search" from the package's exclusions. Stands: no JavaScript in the data plane, no relevance ranking, no identity provider in the engine.
- **2026-09-12 — expiry, assets and jobs move onto the doing-list** (author: "complete snapback4 to the point where the entire clique benchmark can be run"). What it unblocks: the struck half of the Clique brief (M4 media, M5 view-once and expiry with no client open, M8's scheduled digest). Taken off in the same change: the "one photo path" and "cron syntax" exclusions above narrow to transcoding and to cron beyond `every N [at HH:MM]`; the "time in rules" exclusion stands, answered by `expire at .col` rather than a rule.
- **2026-09-13 — native jobs on (author: "write up an LLP about this and then implement").** Unblocks the scoring half of a feed — floats, vectors, real loops, a typed schema — without putting any of it into Quarry, and gives the model half of LLP 3000.004 a seat inside the bounds: one chunk per commit, the job ceilings, fuel, no I/O. Off the doing-list in the same change: the "external ranker with a service seat" of LLP 3000.004 §6.5 is no longer the only shape for compute over the store; it remains the shape for the network. Ranked and vector search, effects execution and an embedded JS engine stay above.
- **2026-09-13 — `sql`, a fifth named observability verb, moves onto the doing-list** (author ruling on LLP 3000.007 §14.10). Read-only SQL over generated per-table views of the developer's own store, under `dev` or against a `--release` directory; never rule-filtered, never an application surface. What it unblocks: the ground truth two Clique essays said Snapback lacked beside Postgres ("there is no underlying Postgres to query"), and the inspection the 0.2.6 Astra lane did by copying its SQLite file. Taken off in the same change: SQL reads as an application query surface (LLP 3000.007 §9.1) leave the doing-list until the reporting gap is measured after the language relaxations; reporting is Quarry's, inspection is `sql`'s. Stands: no JavaScript in the data plane, one authoring language.

- **2026-09-14 — the simulator witness is published for app builders (LLP 3000.007 §20.10, S30).** Unblocks native offline proof artifacts; replaces the repository-only Metro witness on the doing-list. Real-browser and device witnesses still cover only what the deterministic simulator cannot reach.

- **2026-09-14 — development clock control (S27, calibration F5)** moves onto the doing-list to unblock expiry and scheduled-digest tests without real-minute waits or backdated seeds; waiting on real time leaves the development test path, while production clock controls stay off the doing-list.

- **2026-09-25 — ephemeral tables enact the standing realtime line of LLP 3000.009 §12 (LLP 3000.017).** Unblocks typing and viewing without durable outbox traffic. Nothing leaves the doing-list: this enacts an already admitted scope. Last-seen storage, multi-server presence, a separate presence stream and ephemeral authority over durable invariants remain excluded.

- **2026-09-30 — bounded client subscription inspection (author's PR round-0 task)**
  moves onto the doing-list: query-group queue/in-flight/withdrawal counts and
  bounded latency/cause samples explain mounted screens flashing empty. Taken off
  the doing-list: builders must reconstruct this pressure from ad-hoc console
  instrumentation. General observability beyond the named verbs remains excluded;
  there is no telemetry transport or server admin console (LLP 3000.023 §10).

# Rules

**Snapback 2 optimizes the edit-to-verified loop — the agent's building an app on it, and ours building it.**

Speed is the constraint. Everything below exists to keep the edit-to-verified loop short
and to stop this repository accreting apparatus faster than anyone can remove it. These
rules bind `snapback2/` and the LLPs numbered 1000 and up; Snapback 1 is baselined, not
exempt, and its numbers may only fall.

Each rule is **[check]** (enforced by `caps`) or **[review]** (enforced by a human).

## Budgets — every budget is a trade, not a limit

- **5 blocking checks, 60s total.** A sixth requires deleting one, in the same PR. **[check]**
- **59 documents in the working set** (`llp/current/`). Today's count. A 60th requires
  archiving one — which is just removing the link. Snapback 2 aims to leave this at 15;
  Snapback 1's links are archived at promotion. **[check]**
- **12 documents in the foundation** (`llp/foundation/`). **[check]**
- **This file: 700 words.** If it grows, something becomes a check or stops being a rule. **[check]**
- **1,500 lines per source file, baseline 204.** Generated files exempt — and generated
  files are built, not committed; so are benchmark run records under `benchmarks/runs/`,
  which are evidence, not source. The baseline is Snapback 1's oversize count on the day
  the rule landed; it may not grow, and `snapback2/` contributes zero to it. **[check]**

## Blocking checks

`caps` · `ref-check` · `snapback2/scripts/test.sh` · `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs --check` · `check-inventories`

## Loop shape

- **Every check reports all failures in one run.** Fail-fast is banned. **[check]**
- **Nothing blocks on anything slower than 60 seconds.** Slow verification runs on a
  schedule, attributed to the breaking commit, and files a bounded set of issues. **[review]**
- **Fix loops get 3 rounds.** Then stop: escalate to a human or descope. **[review]**

## Time budgets

Tracked every run of `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs` (appends `snapback2/metrics/loop.jsonl`).
A regression is a P0 with a name on it.

| | budget |
|---|---|
| Incremental rebuild after a one-line edit | 15s |
| Test what you just changed | 30s |
| Blocking gate suite | 60s |
| Full build, warm cache | 5 min |
| **`snapback2 check` on a program (the agent's product latency)** | **1s** |
| **`snapback2 doctor` boot-to-ready** | **0.5s** |

## Scope

- **`NOT-DOING.md` is binding.** Moving something onto the doing-list means writing why
  and taking something off. **[review]**
- **Delete; don't deprecate.** No compat shims or migration paths before promotion. **[review]**
- **Nothing is compiled, transpiled, or generated at runtime that could be built ahead of
  time.** **[review]**
- **A spec needs an implementer and a date, or it isn't written.** **[review]**
- **Only implemented specs bind.** A document with no running code behind it is a
  proposal, and a proposal cannot block a PR or justify a check. **[review]**

## Agents

- **Agents remove apparatus freely and add none.** An agent PR that adds a check, script,
  registry, config file, or design doc needs explicit human approval saying so. **[review]**
- **2026-09-06 session exception:** the user delegated the search implementation
  decisions; one `snapback2-core/build.rs` may generate pinned Unicode tables at
  build time, alongside the existing package build. No new gate, registry,
  runtime generator, or Unicode dependency is authorized by this exception. **[review]**
- **Snapback 2 LLPs are numbered 1000 and up**; `llp-create` must be told. **[review]**
- **Snapback 4 LLPs are numbered 3000 and up** (`snapback4/`, LLP 3000); it adopts these budgets
  and loop shape as its own and keeps its scope in `snapback4/NOT-DOING.md`. **[review]**

## Shared machines

- Warm, named lanes, one per stream of work. Never clone fresh; reuse the worktree.
- **Never `git stash`.** Use a temporary commit.
- Kill only PIDs you recorded at launch. Never by name or pattern.

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/program/aggregate_facts.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/program/aggregate_facts.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..10002e01ee
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/program/aggregate_facts.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,166 @@
+//! Exact non-empty facts established by successful count guards.
+
+use super::*;
+use std::collections::BTreeSet;
+
+pub(super) const NONEMPTY: &str = "$aggregateNonempty";
+/// Capture marker for a local whose current value is an exact `count(domain)`
+/// observation. It lives on the result and every domain root: ordinary
+/// rebinding, a write, an authority edge, or a control-flow meet therefore
+/// destroys stale provenance without repurposing diagnostic `origins`.
+pub(super) const COUNT_CAPTURE: &str = "$aggregateCountCapture";
+
+impl Binder<'_> {
+    /// A non-empty observation survives evaluation of its guard only when the
+    /// complete condition is write-free. Unlike point facts, aggregate facts
+    /// deliberately admit filters and seeks because those are part of the
+    /// exact domain identity recorded below.
+    pub(super) fn aggregate_guard_safe(&self, value: &A) -> bool {
+        match value {
+            A::Name { .. } | A::Focal { .. } | A::Literal { .. } => true,
+            A::Array { items, .. } => items.iter().all(|item| self.aggregate_guard_safe(item)),
+            A::Object { fields, .. } => fields.iter().all(|field| field.value.as_ref().is_none_or(|value| self.aggregate_guard_safe(value))),
+            A::Unary { value, .. } | A::Assert { value, .. } | A::ShapeUse { base: value, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(value),
+            A::Binary { left, right, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(left) && self.aggregate_guard_safe(right),
+            A::Member { base, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(base),
+            A::Call { name, args, .. } => self.catalog.functions.get(name).is_none_or(|function|
+                self.pure_functions.get(&function.name) == Some(&true))
+                && args.iter().all(|arg| self.aggregate_guard_safe(arg)),
+            A::Read(read) | A::Exists { read, .. } | A::Created { read, .. } => {
+                read.computed.values().all(|value| self.aggregate_guard_safe(value))
+                    && read.keys.iter().all(|key| self.aggregate_guard_safe(&key.value))
+                    && read.seeks.iter().all(|seek| self.aggregate_guard_safe(&seek.value))
+                    && read.filter.as_deref().is_none_or(|filter| self.aggregate_guard_safe(filter))
+                    && read.matching.as_deref().is_none_or(|matching| self.aggregate_guard_safe(matching))
+                    && read.range.as_ref().and_then(|range| range.cursor.as_deref()).is_none_or(|cursor| self.aggregate_guard_safe(cursor))
+            }
+            A::Shape { base, fields, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(base)
+                && fields.iter().all(|field| match field {
+                    ShapeField::Field { value, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(value),
+                    ShapeField::Spread { .. } | ShapeField::NamedSpread { .. } | ShapeField::Bare { .. } => true,
+                }),
+            A::If { then, condition, otherwise, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(then)
+                && self.aggregate_guard_safe(condition)
+                && self.aggregate_guard_safe(otherwise),
+            A::Merge(_) | A::Walk { .. } | A::Write { .. } => false,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Record only implications that follow from count's nonnegative range.
+    /// The common authored form is `require n > 0`, where `n` was bound from
+    /// `count(domain)`; direct count calls use the same identity.
+    // @ref LLP 3000.013.001#4-non-empty-domain-proof — the fact belongs to the exact domain roots and transaction state.
+    pub(super) fn record_aggregate_nonempty(&mut self, condition: &A, truth: bool) {
+        if !truth { return; }
+        let A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } = condition else { return };
+        let (candidate, threshold, op) = if let Some(n) = literal_int(right) {
+            (left.as_ref(), n, op.as_str())
+        } else if let Some(n) = literal_int(left) {
+            let reversed = match op.as_str() { "<" => ">", "<=" => ">=", ">" => "<", ">=" => "<=", other => other };
+            (right.as_ref(), n, reversed)
+        } else { return };
+        let proves_positive = match op {
+            ">" => threshold >= 0,
+            ">=" | "=" => threshold >= 1,
+            "!=" => threshold == 0,
+            _ => false,
+        };
+        if !proves_positive { return; }
+        let Some((key, roots)) = self.count_key(candidate) else { return };
+        for root in roots {
+            let Some(mut binding) = self.binding(&root).cloned() else { return };
+            binding.fields.insert(key.clone(), Ty::Bool);
+            self.scopes.last_mut().expect("a scope").insert(root, binding);
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn aggregate_nonempty(&self, read: &ReadExpr) -> bool {
+        self.aggregate_key(read).is_some_and(|(key, roots)| roots.iter().all(|root|
+            self.binding(root).is_some_and(|binding| binding.fields.get(&key) == Some(&Ty::Bool))))
+    }
+
+    /// Resolve count provenance before rebinding `name`: a count domain may
+    /// itself refer to the old value of that local. Such a self-dependent
+    /// capture cannot be represented by the post-assignment binding and is
+    /// therefore deliberately not narrowed.
+    pub(super) fn count_capture(&self, name: &str, value: &A) -> Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)> {
+        let A::Call { name: call, args, .. } = value else { return None };
+        if call != "count" || args.len() != 1 || self.catalog.functions.contains_key(call)
+            || !self.aggregate_guard_safe(value) { return None; }
+        let read = args.first().and_then(|arg| self.aggregate_domain(arg))?;
+        let (aggregate, roots) = self.aggregate_key(&read)?;
+        if roots.contains(name) { return None; }
+        let capture = vec![COUNT_CAPTURE.into(), aggregate[1].clone()];
+        Some((capture, roots))
+    }
+
+    /// Attach pre-resolved capture-time provenance after assigning `name`.
+    /// `origins` remains diagnostic history; this field fact is the reaching
+    /// definition proof used by a later `require name > 0`.
+    pub(super) fn record_count_capture(&mut self, name: &str, capture: Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)>) {
+        let Some((capture, mut owners)) = capture else { return };
+        owners.insert(name.to_owned());
+        for owner in owners {
+            let Some(mut binding) = self.binding(&owner).cloned() else { return };
+            binding.fields.insert(capture.clone(), Ty::Bool);
+            self.scopes.last_mut().expect("a scope").insert(owner, binding);
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn count_key(&self, value: &A) -> Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)> {
+        let (count_arg, captured_name) = match value {
+            A::Call { name, args, .. } if name == "count" && args.len() == 1
+                && !self.catalog.functions.contains_key(name) => args.first(),
+            A::Name { name, .. } => self.binding(name)?.origins.iter().rev().find_map(|(_, origin)| match origin {
+                A::Call { name, args, .. } if name == "count" && args.len() == 1
+                    && !self.catalog.functions.contains_key(name) => args.first(),
+                _ => None,
+            }),
+            _ => None,
+        }.map(|arg| (arg, match value { A::Name { name, .. } => Some(name.as_str()), _ => None }))?;
+        let result = self.aggregate_key(&self.aggregate_domain(count_arg)?)?;
+        if let Some(name) = captured_name {
+            let capture = vec![COUNT_CAPTURE.into(), result.0[1].clone()];
+            if self.binding(name)?.fields.get(&capture) != Some(&Ty::Bool)
+                || !result.1.iter().all(|root| self.binding(root)
+                    .is_some_and(|binding| binding.fields.get(&capture) == Some(&Ty::Bool)))
+            {
+                return None;
+            }
+        }
+        Some(result)
+    }
+
+    fn aggregate_key(&self, read: &ReadExpr) -> Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)> {
+        if read.range.is_some() || read.matching.is_some() { return None; }
+        let mut roots = BTreeSet::new();
+        let keys = read.keys.iter().map(|key| Some(format!("{:?}:{}", key.column,
+            self.aggregate_value(&key.value, &mut roots)?))).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?;
+        let seeks = read.seeks.iter().map(|seek| Some(format!("{}:{}:{}", seek.column, seek.op,
+            self.aggregate_value(&seek.value, &mut roots)?))).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?;
+        let filter = match read.filter.as_deref() {
+            Some(value) => Some(self.aggregate_value(value, &mut roots)?),
+            None => None,
+        };
+        if roots.is_empty() { roots.insert(pure_calls::CONSTANTS.into()); }
+        let identity = format!("{:?}:{:?}:{:?}:{keys:?}:{seeks:?}:{filter:?}", read.table, read.index, read.order_keys);
+        Some((vec![NONEMPTY.into(), identity], roots))
+    }
+
+    fn aggregate_value(&self, value: &A, roots: &mut BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<String> {
+        match value {
+            A::Focal { .. } => Some("focal".into()),
+            A::Member { base, name, .. } if matches!(base.as_ref(), A::Focal { .. }) => Some(format!("focal.{name}")),
+            A::Literal { .. } | A::Name { .. } | A::Member { .. } => self.stable_value(value, roots).map(|value| value.key()),
+            A::Unary { op, value, .. } => Some(format!("unary:{op}:{}", self.aggregate_value(value, roots)?)),
+            A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } => Some(format!("binary:{op}:{}:{}", self.aggregate_value(left, roots)?, self.aggregate_value(right, roots)?)),
+            A::Call { name, args, .. } => {
+                let function = self.catalog.functions.get(name)?;
+                if self.pure_functions.get(&function.name) != Some(&true) { return None; }
+                Some(format!("call:{name}:{:?}", args.iter().map(|arg| self.aggregate_value(arg, roots)).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?))
+            }
+            A::Array { items, .. } => Some(format!("array:{:?}", items.iter().map(|item| self.aggregate_value(item, roots)).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?)),
+            _ => None,
+        }
+    }
+}

### 3.2 Maintained views: aggregates

```quarry
view followerCount: count follows by .followedId
view receivedLikes: count likes by .postId.authorId
view dailyPosts: count posts where not .removed by .authorId, day(.at)
view revenue: sum orders of .amount by .shopId

table posts:
  likeCount: count likes
```

These have exactly the semantics of today's maintains: the same engine, the
same recorded attribution, and maintained columns for the in-table form.
`followerCount[p]` reads the number, 0 when absent. Two defaults remove the
boilerplate lines:

- **Readability is derived.** A uniformly readable source gives a readable
  aggregate. A source whose read rule uses only bare group keys gives the same
  rule over the aggregate's key. Anything else needs an explicit `read <-`.
- **In-table columns find their reference.** A column is counted by the one
  column of the source that references the table. If there are several, use
  `count likes by .postId`.

### 3.3 Materialized views: Following
### 5.1 Streaming aggregates

`count(R)`, `sum(R, .col)` and `exists R`, where `R` is a predicate read
without a page clause, examine rows under the examined and steps meters.
Each decoded row is charged transiently, and exactly that charge is released
when the row is dropped. Retained state stays charged.

A streaming consumer keeps the underlying scan's admission, authorization,
expiry and coverage checks. Calling a scan `count` does not make it a safe
probe; LLP 3000.007 §21.9's expiring-mutation counterexample stands.
Unpaged aggregate reads retain ordinary streaming scans: membership, enum
complements and window predicates do not become bounded merge pages. Their
residual filters fold the entire admitted domain, or return null on a cut.
Streaming aggregation across planned lanes is not implemented.

The busy-chat digest claim (LLP 3000.011.001.000's 16 MiB stop) holds only
if the retained recipient-heavy fixture passes.

An inferred aggregate seek must preserve predicate short-circuiting: its
endpoint must already be present and must not fail when evaluated before the
whole predicate. Otherwise the comparison stays a residual filter. Selecting
one safe endpoint must not extract an unsafe sibling bound on the same column.
A named prefix pinning intrinsic `id` keeps its single-row access path; remaining
comparisons filter that row rather than introducing an order after the id pin.

### 5.2 Self-chunking jobs
### 14.7 A hidden keyed maintained value is unavailable, including at zero

A keyed maintained point authorizes the requested group before disclosing
whether storage contains it. If admitted, a stored group returns its value and
an absent group returns the maintained operation's identity, currently zero
for `count` and `sum`. If the point's read rule hides the group, a stored group
and an absent group both return `null`; the absent case must never fall through
the authorized-miss coercion and become zero. A query may instead `require` the
same authority condition first and return its chosen refusal code.

The authorization decision is identical for stored and synthetic groups even
when the aggregate's source expires. The actual system principal bypasses the view
rule for a synthetic miss just as it does for a stored hit, and therefore sees
the identity. That policy bypass does not bypass a read-through parent's
lifetime: an inherited group remains nullable until an exact live-parent point
witness proves the parent exists. A row yielded by a fresh table read can carry
that witness through a loop only when the whole loop body is proven write-free;
saved or buffered row values do not renew it, and a writeful loop needs a
current point guard in each iteration.
Because an unguarded private point can return `null`, its static result is a
nullable number. A matching effect-safe authority proof may narrow that result
to the maintained operation's required numeric type. Maintained-rule focal
fields stay scoped to the maintained target row; only declared group fields
are replaced with caller key expressions, so an unrelated caller projection
cannot supply a target-only rule field. A
write, relevant rebinding, or entry into and exit from a viewer-scoped block
invalidates that proof; a job inside `as principal` has that principal's
authority rather than the system exemption. Loop headers retain only facts
that survive every iteration, including facts on an outer binding while a
loop item shadows its source name, separately from local assignment revisions.
Program `exists` observes only rows readable by its current viewer, while an
`exists` witness inside the maintained rule tests raw presence below the
target table's read rule. A positive program witness therefore proves raw
presence, but a negative one proves raw absence only for the actual system
scope, a uniformly readable target, or a complete point key whose selected row
is structurally readable. Matching text alone does not turn a hidden miss into
a raw-absence authority proof. Authored rule constants are resolved before
group-key expressions are substituted. A parameter, local or loop item named
`allow`, `public` or `deny` remains a lexical operand rather than acquiring the
rule constant's meaning.

`check` emits `N_MAINTAIN_AUTHORIZATION` when a query directly returns a bare,
fully keyed maintained point whose read rule is narrower than the set of query
callers and no dominating `require` proves the same authority condition for

   196	                if name == "length" && matches!(t.required(), Ty::Text(_) | Ty::List(..) | Ty::Page(..) | Ty::Collection(..)) {
   197	                    return Err(unsupported(site, ".length", format!("count({})", print::expression(base))));
   198	                }
   199	                // @ref LLP 3000.036#12 — a required reference's field reads its row:
   200	                // `x.ref.col` is `t[x.ref].col`, the same authorized point read
   201	                // (null when the row is missing or hidden), bound once.
   202	                // A recorded attribution column spelled `ref.col` names the value
   203	                // copied at insert; the live read would be a second meaning.
   204	                let recorded = matches!(base.as_ref(), A::Member { name: column, .. }
   205	                    if self.catalog.tables.values().any(|info| info.recorded.contains_key(&format!("{column}.{name}"))));
   206	                if let Ty::Ref(table) = &t && name != "id" && !recorded
   207	                    && self.catalog.tables.get(table).is_some_and(|info| info.maintained.is_none() && info.decl.ephemeral.is_none())
   208	                {
   209	                    let local = self.temp("reference");
   210	                    let runtime = self.declare(&local, t.clone());
   211	                    out.push(Stmt::Const { name: runtime, value: e });
   212	                    let key = ast::KeyPart { column: None, value: A::Name { name: local, site: site.clone() }, site: site.clone() };
   213	                    let read = ReadExpr { cursor_prefix: None, computed: Default::default(), order_keys: Vec::new(), table: table.clone(), keys: vec![key], index: None, range: None, matching: None, filter: None, seeks: Vec::new(), site: site.clone() };
   214	                    return self.computation(&A::Member { base: Box::new(A::Read(read)), name: name.clone(), site: site.clone() }, out);
   215	                }
   216	                // @ref LLP 3000.036#13.7 — `x.ref.col` reads one reference. A second hop
   217	                // (`r.planting.bed.owner`) gets the two steps that compile, by name.
   218	                if let Ty::Ref(target) = t.required() && t.is_optional() && name != "id"
   219	                    && let Some(rewrite) = self.second_hop_rewrite(base, &target, name) {
   220	                    return Err(type_error(site, format!("`{}` reads two references; `x.ref.col` reads one ({} may be missing or hidden)", print::expression(expr), print::expression(base)), rewrite).guide("shapes"));
   221	                }
   222	                let (value, ty) = self.member(e, t, name, site)?;
   223	                Ok((value, self.field_refinement(expr).unwrap_or(ty)))
   224	            }
   225	            A::Call { name, args, .. } => {
   226	                let (value, ty) = self.call(name, args, site, out)?;
   227	                self.record_call(expr, &ty);
   228	                Ok((value, self.call_refinement(expr).unwrap_or(ty)))
   229	            },
   230	            A::Read(read) if read.table == "connected" && !self.catalog.tables.contains_key("connected") => self.connected(read, out),
   231	            A::Read(read) => {
   232	                let (value, ty) = self.read(read, out)?;
   233	                Ok((value, if self.point_present(read) { ty.required() } else { ty }))
   234	            },
   235	            A::Merge(merge) => self.merge(merge, out),
   236	            A::Exists { read, .. } if read.table == "connected" && !self.catalog.tables.contains_key("connected") => {
   237	                let (count, _) = self.connected(read, out)?;
   238	                Ok((Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::Gt, left: Box::new(count), right: Box::new(Expr::Literal(Value::Int(0))) }, Ty::Bool))
   239	            }
   240	            A::Exists { read, .. } => {
   241	                self.exists_read(read, out)
   242	            }
   243	            A::Created { .. } => Err(unknown(site, "created is valid only in an insert table rule", "use exists here")),
   244	            A::Assert { value, code, message, .. } => {
   245	                validate_code(site, code)?;
   246	                let (mut e, t) = self.expr(value, out)?;
   247	                // A row point may return null because its read meter cut. Do
   248	                // not turn that unavailable fact into an authored NOT_FOUND.
   249	                if self.caller_kind == ProgramKind::Query && t.is_optional() && matches!(t.required(), Ty::Row(_)) {
   250	                    e = Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::RequireUncapped, args: vec![e] };
   251	                }
   252	                let tmp = self.temp("present");
   253	                out.push(Stmt::Let { name: tmp.clone(), value: e });
   254	                out.push(Stmt::Require { condition: Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::Ne, left: Box::new(ir::var(&tmp)), right: Box::new(Expr::Literal(Value::Null)) }, code: code.clone(), site: Some(site.to_string()), message: message.clone() });
   255	                if let A::Read(read) = value.as_ref() { self.narrow_point(read); }
   256	                Ok((ir::var(&tmp), t.required()))
   257	            }
   258	            A::Shape { base, fields, .. } => self.shape(base, fields, site, out),
   259	            A::ShapeUse { base, name, .. } => {
   260	                let Some(shape) = self.catalog.shapes.get(name).cloned() else {
   261	                    return Err(unknown(site, format!("unknown shape {name}"), name_rewrite(name, self.catalog.shapes.keys().map(String::as_str), Some("declare `shape name = { fields }`"))));
   262	                };
   263	                self.shape(base, &shape.fields, site, out)
   264	            }
   265	            A::Walk { table, seed, column, depth, .. } => {
   266	                let (recurse, ty) = self.walk(table, seed, column, *depth, site, out)?;
   267	                let list = self.temp("walk");
   268	                out.push(Stmt::Let { name: list.clone(), value: Expr::Array(Vec::new()) });
   269	                let item = self.temp("node");
   270	                out.push(Stmt::For { binding: item.clone(), domain: LoopDomain::Recurse(recurse), body: vec![Stmt::Push { target: list.clone(), value: ir::var(&item) }] });
   271	                Ok((ir::var(&list), Ty::List(Box::new(ty), depth.saturating_add(1))))
   272	            }
   273	            A::Write { .. } => self.write(expr, out, true).map(|opt| opt.expect("a valued write")),
   274	        }
   275	    }
   276	
   277	    /// `connected[p]`: how many connections the principal holds open on the
   278	    /// server now, an int; `exists connected[p]` is the bool. Not a table:
   279	    /// the server's registry of long polls answers it, a device answers 1
   280	    /// and marks its read, and the server decides the write.
   281	    fn connected(&mut self, read: &ReadExpr, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
   282	        let site = &read.site;
   283	        if read.keys.len() != 1 || read.range.is_some() || read.matching.is_some() || read.index.is_some() {
   284	            return Err(unknown(site, "connected takes one principal: connected[p] counts its connections, exists connected[p] tests", "exists connected[m.principal]"));
   285	        }
   286	        let key = &read.keys[0];
   287	        let (e, t) = self.expr_as_identity(&key.value, out, &Ty::Principal)?;
   288	        if !matches!(t.required(), Ty::Principal | Ty::Id) {
   289	            return Err(type_error(key.value.site(), format!("connected takes a principal, got {}", t.name()), "connected[m.principal]"));
   290	        }
   291	        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.1 — retain the author's deciding read alongside the IR, never in its serialized form.
   292	        self.presence_sources.push((e.clone(), site.clone(), print::read_expr(read)));
   293	        self.sources.insert(format!("presence/{site}"), (site.clone(), print::read_expr(read)));
   294	        Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Connected, args: vec![e] }, Ty::Int))
   295	    }
   296	
   297	    pub(super) fn name(&mut self, name: &str, site: &Site) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
   298	        match name {
   299	            "viewer" | "$input:viewer" => Ok((Expr::Input(Input::Viewer), Ty::Principal)),
   300	            "now" | "commit" => {
   301	                if self.kind == ProgramKind::Query && name == "commit" {
   302	                    return Err(unknown(site, "commit is the mutation commit clock; queries read now", "now"));
   303	                }
   304	                Ok((Expr::Input(Input::Now), Ty::Time))
   305	            }
   306	            "new" => {
   307	                if self.viewer_depth.is_some() { return Err(job_reads::read_only(site)); }
   308	                if self.kind == ProgramKind::Query {
   309	                    return Err(unknown(site, "queries cannot mint ids", "mint ids in a mutation"));
   310	                }
   311	                Ok((Expr::Input(Input::NewId), Ty::Id))
   312	            }
   313	            "true" => Ok((Expr::Literal(Value::Bool(true)), Ty::Bool)),
   314	            "false" => Ok((Expr::Literal(Value::Bool(false)), Ty::Bool)),
   315	            "null" => Ok((Expr::Literal(Value::Null), Ty::Null)),
   316	            _ => {
   317	                if let Some(binding) = self.binding(name) {
   318	                    if let Some(error) = &binding.error { return Err(error.clone()); }
   319	                    return Ok((ir::var(&binding.runtime), binding.ty.clone()));
   320	                }
   321	                if self.catalog.tables.contains_key(name) {
   322	                    return Err(unknown(site, format!("{name} is a table; a read needs a key or a range"), format!("{name}[key]  -- or: {name}[prefix] first 50 by index")));
   323	                }
   324	                let declared: Vec<&str> = self.scopes.iter().flat_map(|s| s.keys().map(String::as_str)).chain(["viewer", "now", "new"]).collect();
   325	                Err(unknown(site, format!("unknown name {name}"), name_rewrite(name, declared, None)))
   326	            }
   327	        }
   328	    }
   329	
   330	    /// The type of `expr` without binding it into this program.
   331	    fn speculative_type(&self, expr: &A) -> Option<Ty> {
   332	        let mut probe = self.clone();
   333	        probe.computation(expr, &mut setup::Body::default()).ok().map(|(_, ty)| ty)
   334	    }
   335	
   336	    /// A local name for the row a reference column names, unused in scope.
   337	    fn row_local(&self, column: &str) -> String {
   338	        let taken = |name: &str| self.scopes.iter().any(|scope| scope.contains_key(name)) || self.catalog.tables.contains_key(name);
   339	        let mut name = column.to_owned();
   340	        if taken(&name) { name.push_str("Row"); }
   341	        while taken(&name) { name.push('_'); }
   342	        name
   343	    }
   344	
   345	    /// `x.a.b.c` where `x.a` is a required reference: read the `a` row, then one hop.
   346	    fn second_hop_rewrite(&self, base: &A, target: &str, field: &str) -> Option<String> {
   347	        let A::Member { base: inner, name: hop, .. } = base else { return None };
   348	        let Some(Ty::Ref(first)) = self.speculative_type(inner).filter(|ty| !ty.is_optional()) else { return None };
   349	        let reference = print::expression(inner);
   350	        let row = self.row_local(inner_name(inner).unwrap_or(&first));
   351	        let mut second = self.row_local(hop);
   352	        if second == row { second.push_str("Row"); }
   353	        Some(format!("read the first row, then one hop: `{row} = {first}[{reference}] ! else NOT_FOUND`, then `{row}.{hop}.{field}` (null when the {target} row is missing or hidden); for a present value read that row too: `{second} = {target}[{row}.{hop}] ! else NOT_FOUND`, then `{second}.{field}`"))
   354	    }
   355	
   356	    /// `p.bed.max` compared in `op`: read the `bed` row present first, then compare its field.
   357	    fn present_row_rewrite(&self, operand: &A, op: &str, left: &A, right: &A) -> Option<String> {
   358	        let A::Member { base, name: field, .. } = operand else { return None };
   359	        let Some(Ty::Ref(table)) = self.speculative_type(base).filter(|ty| !ty.is_optional()) else { return None };
   360	        let row = self.row_local(inner_name(base).unwrap_or(&table));
   361	        let read = print::expression(base);
   362	        let compared = |side: &A| if std::ptr::eq(side, operand) { format!("{row}.{field}") } else { print::expression(side) };
   363	        Some(format!("read the row present first, so a missing or hidden one refuses instead of passing: `{row} = {table}[{read}] ! else NOT_FOUND`, then compare `{} {op} {}` (`?? 0` would treat a missing row as 0)", compared(left), compared(right)))
   364	    }
   365	
   366	    pub(super) fn member(&mut self, base: Expr, ty: Ty, name: &str, site: &Site) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
   367	        let field_ty = match ty.required() {
   368	            Ty::WriteRow(table) => {
   369	                let info = self.table(&table, site)?;
   370	                if super::super::columns::fields(info).any(|f|f == name) {
   371	                    return Err(Diagnostic::new(site,"E_MAINTAINED_COLUMN_RESULT",format!("{table}.{name} is absent from a write result"),"read the row under its read rule").guide("maintains"));
   372	                }
   373	                return self.member(base, if ty.is_optional() { Ty::Row(table).optional() } else { Ty::Row(table) }, name, site);
   374	            }
   375	            Ty::Row(table) => {
   376	                let info = self.table(&table, site)?;
   377	                // @ref LLP 3000.007#23 — count is an alias of the certified
   378	                // value, except when the view declares a real count column.
   379	                if name == "count" && !info.columns.contains_key(name)
   380	                    && info.maintained.as_ref().is_some_and(|m| m.aggregate == "count") {
   381	                    return self.member(base, ty, "value", site);
   382	                }
   383	                // @ref LLP 3000.015#3 — check the receiver's static row type
   384	                // before lowering can erase helper or returned-data position.
   385	                if !self.returned_data || self.depth > 0 || (name != "id" && name != "pending" && !info.columns.contains_key(name)) {
   386	                    super::super::row_views::predicate_field(info, name, site)?;
   387	                }
   388	                if name == "pending" && self.returned_data && info.maintained.as_ref().is_some_and(|m| m.row_key.is_some()) {
   389	                    return Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::OptionalField { field: name.into() }, args: vec![base] }, Ty::Bool.optional()));
   390	                }
   391	                if let Some(column) = info.decl.columns.iter().find(|column| column.name == name && column.written_by.is_some() && !column.readable_by_audience) {
   392	                    return Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::OptionalField { field: name.into() }, args: vec![base] }, Ty::from_scalar(&column.type_).optional()));
   393	                }
   394	                if name == "id" {
   395	                    Ty::Ref(table.clone())
   396	                } else {
   397	                    match info.columns.get(name) {
   398	                        Some(scalar) => Ty::from_scalar(scalar),
   399	                        None => return Err(unknown(site, format!("{table} has no column {name}"), name_rewrite(name, info.columns.keys().map(String::as_str).chain(["id"]), None))),
   400	                    }
   401	                }
   402	            }
   403	            Ty::Object(fields) | Ty::RowShape(fields) | Ty::RowObject(fields) => match fields.get(name) {
   404	                Some(field) => field.clone(),
   405	                None => return Err(unknown(site, format!("this object has no field {name}"), name_rewrite(name, fields.keys().map(String::as_str), None))),
   406	            },
   407	            Ty::Ref(table) => {
   408	                // @ref LLP 3000.007#18.5 — a reference needs an explicit row lookup or the shape's implicit row parameter.
   409	                let reference = match &base {
   410	                    Expr::Variable(runtime) => self.scopes.iter().rev().find_map(|scope| scope.iter().find(|(_, binding)| &binding.runtime == runtime).map(|(name, _)| name.as_str())).unwrap_or("reference"),
   411	                    _ => "reference",
   412	                };
   413	                return Err(type_error(site, format!("a {table} reference has no fields"),
   414	                    format!("{table}[{reference}] ! else NOT_FOUND — read the row, or use the shape's row parameter: {table}[{reference}] {{ {name}: .{name} }}")).guide("shapes"));
   415	            }
   416	            Ty::Image | Ty::Video => match name {
   417	                "id" => Ty::Id,
   418	                "width" | "height" | "duration" => Ty::Int.optional(),
   419	                "bytes" => Ty::Int,
   420	                "type" => Ty::Text(64),
   421	                _ => return Err(unknown(site, format!("assets have no field {name}"), "id, width, height, bytes, type, duration")),
   422	            },
   423	            Ty::File => match name {
   424	                "id" => Ty::Id,
   425	                "bytes" => Ty::Int,
   426	                "type" => Ty::Text(128),
   427	                "name" => Ty::Text(snapback4_core::assets::MAX_NAME_BYTES as u32),
   428	                _ => return Err(unknown(site, format!("files have no field {name}"), "id, bytes, type, name")),
   429	            },
   430	            // A scalar already *is* the value, so the repair is to drop the field access,
   431	            // not to go and find a row. `int has no fields` was the most frequent compile
   432	            // error of the 0.2.28 calibration — 20 of its 32 E_QUARRY_TYPE — and the
   433	            // generic advice pointed away from the fix: a full group-key `maintain`
   434	            // lookup is its count, and the author had written `.value` on it.
   435	            // `Ty::Id` keeps the old advice: an id is exactly the case where a row read
   436	            // is what is missing.
   437	            other @ (Ty::Bool | Ty::Int | Ty::Time | Ty::Decimal(_) | Ty::Money(..) | Ty::Text(_) | Ty::Principal | Ty::Enum(_)) => {
   438	                return Err(type_error(site, format!("{} has no fields", other.name()), format!("this is already a value — remove `.{name}`")));
   439	            }
   440	            other => return Err(type_error(site, format!("{} has no fields", other.name()), "read a row or an object before selecting a field")),
   441	        };
   442	        let result_ty = if ty.is_optional() { field_ty.optional() } else { field_ty };
   443	        Ok((ir::field(base, name), result_ty))
   444	    }
   445	
   446	    pub(super) fn binary(&mut self, op: &str, left: &A, right: &A, site: &Site, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
   447	        if op == "in" {
   448	            let (value, ty) = self.expr(left, out)?;
   449	            let value = self.snapshot(value, out);
   450	            let (domain, item) = self.loop_domain(right, out)?;
   451	            if !ty.comparable(&item) { return Err(type_error(site, format!("in compares {} with {}", ty.name(), item.name()), "use a list of values of the column's type")); }
   452	            let found = self.temp("contains");
   453	            let binding = self.temp("member");
   454	            out.push(Stmt::Let { name: found.clone(), value: ir::lit(Value::Bool(false)) });
   455	            let body = vec![Stmt::If { condition: Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::Eq, left: Box::new(value), right: Box::new(ir::var(&binding)) },
   456	                then_body: vec![Stmt::Assign { name: found.clone(), value: ir::lit(Value::Bool(true)) }, Stmt::Break], else_body: Vec::new() }];
   457	            out.push(Stmt::For { binding, domain, body });
   458	            return Ok((ir::var(&found), Ty::Bool));
   459	        }
   460	        if op == "??" {
   461	            let (l, lt) = self.expr(left, out)?;
   462	            let tmp = self.temp("or");
   463	            out.push(Stmt::Let { name: tmp.clone(), value: l });
   464	            let mut fallback = setup::Body::default();
   465	            // `conversationId ?? 'dm1'`: a text literal after an identity is
   466	            // an id, as it is beside `=` and in a key.
   467	            let (r, rt) = if lt.required().is_identity() { self.expr_as_identity(right, &mut fallback, &lt.required())? } else { self.expr(right, &mut fallback)? };
   468	            fallback.push(Stmt::Assign { name: tmp.clone(), value: r });
   469	            out.push_if(Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::Eq, left: Box::new(ir::var(&tmp)), right: Box::new(Expr::Literal(Value::Null)) }, fallback, setup::Body::default());
   470	            let joined = self.join(&lt.required(), &rt, left, right)?;
   471	            let ty = if rt.is_optional() { joined } else { joined.required() };
   472	            return Ok((ir::var(&tmp), ty));
   473	        }
   474	        let (l, lt) = self.expr(left, out)?;
   475	        if op == "and" || op == "or" {
   476	            let result = self.temp("bool");
   477	            out.push(Stmt::Let { name: result.clone(), value: l });
   478	            let mut branch = setup::Body::default();
   479	            self.push_scope();
   480	            self.narrow(left, op == "and");
   481	            let right = self.expr(right, &mut branch);
   482	            self.pop_scope();
   483	            let (r, rt) = right?;
   484	            if !lt.is_bool() || !rt.is_bool() {
   485	                return Err(type_error(site, format!("{op} needs bool operands; got {} and {}", lt.name(), rt.name()), "compare each side first"));
   486	            }
   487	            branch.push(Stmt::Assign { name: result.clone(), value: r });
   488	            let (then_body, else_body) = if op == "and" { (branch, setup::Body::default()) } else { (setup::Body::default(), branch) };
   489	            out.push_if(ir::var(&result), then_body, else_body);
   490	            return Ok((ir::var(&result), Ty::Bool));
   491	        }
   492	        let coerce_right = lt.is_identity();
   493	        let mut right_setup = setup::Body::default();
   494	        let (r, rt) = if coerce_right { self.expr_as_identity(right, &mut right_setup, &lt)? } else { self.expr(right, &mut right_setup)? };
   495	        let (l, lt) = if rt.is_identity() && !lt.is_identity() {
   496	            match (left, &l) {
   497	                (A::Literal { value: Literal::Str(text), .. }, _) => (Expr::Literal(Value::Id(text.clone())), Ty::Id),
   498	                _ => (l, lt),
   499	            }
   500	        } else {
   501	            (l, lt)
   502	        };
   503	        // Work hoisted from the right cannot run before the left value.
   504	        let l = if right_setup.is_empty() {
   505	            l
   506	        } else {
   507	            let left_value = self.temp("left");
   508	            out.push(Stmt::Let { name: left_value.clone(), value: l });
   509	            out.extend(right_setup);
   510	            ir::var(&left_value)
   511	        };
   512	        let focal_nullable = |value: &A, ty: &Ty| self.in_predicate && ty.is_optional()
   513	            && self.focal.as_ref().is_some_and(|(name, ty)| name == "$filter" && matches!(ty, Ty::Row(_)))
   514	            && super::super::intent::column(value).is_some();
   515	        let nullable_left = focal_nullable(left, &lt);
   516	        let nullable_right = focal_nullable(right, &rt);
   517	        let ir_op = match op {
   518	            "/" | "%" => {
   519	                if !matches!(lt, Ty::Int | Ty::Time) || !matches!(rt, Ty::Int | Ty::Time) {
   520	                    return Err(type_error(site, format!("{op} takes present ints or times; got {} and {}", lt.name(), rt.name()), "narrow the operands before division"));
   521	                }
   522	                // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.1 — division shares divmod's Euclidean result and zero refusal.
   523	                let divided = Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Divmod { remainder_sink: "operator".into() }, args: vec![l, r] };
   524	                return Ok((ir::field(divided, if op == "/" { "quotient" } else { "remainder" }), Ty::Int));
   525	            }
   526	            "+" if matches!((&lt, &rt), (Ty::Text(_), Ty::Text(_))) => {
   527	                let (Ty::Text(a), Ty::Text(b)) = (lt, rt) else { unreachable!() };
   528	                // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.1 — text addition uses the shared, heap-metered concatenation builtin.
   529	                return Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Concat, args: vec![l, r] }, Ty::Text(a.saturating_add(b))));
   530	            }
   531	            "+" if matches!((&lt, &rt), (Ty::List(..), Ty::List(..))) => {
   532	                // @ref LLP 3000.019#6 — list construction is an expression, including returns and arguments.
   533	                // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.1 — join items as in literals; Concat charges the full allocation.
   534	                let Ty::List(item, _) = self.join(&lt, &rt, left, right)? else { unreachable!() };
   535	                let (Ty::List(_, a), Ty::List(_, b)) = (lt, rt) else { unreachable!() };
   536	                return Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Concat, args: vec![l, r] }, Ty::List(item, a.saturating_add(b))));
   537	            }
   538	            "+" if matches!(lt.required(), Ty::List(..)) || matches!(rt.required(), Ty::List(..)) => {
   539	                return Err(type_error(site, format!("+ concatenates two lists; got {} and {}", lt.name(), rt.name()),
   540	                    "use `xs + [x]` to append an item; make both lists present with `xs ?? []` if optional"));
   541	            }
   542	            "=" | "!=" => {
   543	                if !lt.comparable(&rt) {
   544	                    if let Some(rewrite) = self.inner_row_rewrite(left, right, &lt, &rt) {
   545	                        return Err(type_error(site, format!("{op} compares {} with {}: inside a predicate, `.` is the predicate's own row, not the enclosing one", lt.name(), rt.name()), rewrite));
   546	                    }
   547	                    return Err(type_error(site, format!("{op} compares {} with {}", lt.name(), rt.name()), "compare values of one type"));
   548	                }
   549	                if op == "=" { BinaryOp::Eq } else { BinaryOp::Ne }
   550	            }
   551	            "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" => {
   552	                if (lt.is_optional() && !nullable_left) || (rt.is_optional() && !nullable_right) {
   553	                    let operand = if lt.is_optional() && !nullable_left { left } else { right };
   554	                    // @ref LLP 3000.036#13.7 — a reference field is optional because its row may be
   555	                    // missing or hidden; `?? 0` would admit then. Read the row present instead (lane 013).
   556	                    if let Some(rewrite) = self.present_row_rewrite(operand, op, left, right) {
   557	                        return Err(type_error(site, format!("{op} needs present operands; `{}` reads a row through a reference, which is null when that row is missing or hidden", print::expression(operand)), rewrite));
   558	                    }
   559	                    return Err(type_error(
   560	                        site,
   561	                        format!("{op} needs present operands; got {} and {}", lt.name(), rt.name()),
   562	                        format!("narrow first: `if {} != null:`, or `{} ?? 0`", print::expression(operand), print::expression(operand)),
   563	                    ));
   564	                }
   565	                if !lt.comparable(&rt) {
   566	                    return Err(type_error(site, format!("{op} compares {} with {}", lt.name(), rt.name()), "compare values of one type"));
   567	                }
   568	                match op {
   569	                    "<" => BinaryOp::Lt,
   570	                    "<=" => BinaryOp::Lte,
   571	                    ">" => BinaryOp::Gt,
   572	                    _ => BinaryOp::Gte,
   573	                }
   574	            }
   575	            "+" | "-" | "*" => {
   576	                if !lt.is_numeric() || !rt.is_numeric() {
   577	                    let optional = if lt.is_optional() { left } else { right };
   578	                    let rewrite = if matches!(optional, A::Call { .. }) && (lt.is_optional() || rt.is_optional()) {
   579	                        let (a, b) = if lt.is_optional() { ("ttl".into(), print::expression(right)) } else { (print::expression(left), "ttl".into()) };
   580	                        format!("bind the optional call once: `ttl = {}`; use `{a} {op} {b} if ttl != null else null`", print::expression(optional))
   581	                    } else if lt.is_optional() || rt.is_optional() {
   582	                        format!("guard `{} != null` before the arithmetic, or choose an explicit default with `{} ?? 0`", print::expression(optional), print::expression(optional))
   583	                    } else { "use int, decimal or money operands for arithmetic".into() };
   584	                    return Err(type_error(site, format!("{op} needs present numbers; got {} and {}", lt.name(), rt.name()), rewrite));
   585	                }
   586	                let result = match (op, &lt, &rt) {
   587	                    ("-", Ty::Time, Ty::Time) => Ty::Int,
   588	                    ("+", Ty::Time, Ty::Int) | ("+", Ty::Int, Ty::Time) | ("-", Ty::Time, Ty::Int) => Ty::Time,
   589	                    ("*", Ty::Time, _) | ("*", _, Ty::Time) => {
   590	                        let left = if lt == Ty::Time { format!("({} / 1)", print::expression(left)) } else { print::expression(left) };
   591	                        let right = if rt == Ty::Time { format!("({} / 1)", print::expression(right)) } else { print::expression(right) };
   592	                        return Err(type_error(site, "* cannot scale a time; use an int number of milliseconds", format!("{left} * {right} — `/ 1` turns a time into int milliseconds; store the scaled count as int. For a server-arrival order keep a per-conversation counter instead: `snapback4 guide arrival`")));
   593	                    }
   594	                    ("+", Ty::Time, Ty::Time) => {
   595	                        return Err(type_error(site, "+ cannot add two times; an offset is an int number of milliseconds", "change the duration parameter or column to int, then add it to the time; subtract two times to measure an elapsed duration"));
   596	                    }
   597	                    (_, Ty::Decimal(a), Ty::Decimal(b)) if a == b && op != "*" => Ty::Decimal(*a),
   598	                    (_, Ty::Money(c, a), Ty::Money(d, b)) if a == b && c == d && op != "*" => Ty::Money(c.clone(), *a),
   599	                    ("*", Ty::Decimal(a), Ty::Int) | ("*", Ty::Int, Ty::Decimal(a)) => Ty::Decimal(*a),
   600	                    ("*", Ty::Money(c, a), Ty::Int) | ("*", Ty::Int, Ty::Money(c, a)) => Ty::Money(c.clone(), *a),
   601	                    (_, Ty::Int, Ty::Int) => Ty::Int,
   602	                    _ => return Err(type_error(site, format!("{op} needs matching numeric types; got {} and {}", lt.name(), rt.name()), "convert one operand")),
   603	                };
   604	                let ir_op = match op {
   605	                    "+" => BinaryOp::Add,
   606	                    "-" => BinaryOp::Sub,
   607	                    _ => BinaryOp::Mul,
   608	                };
   609	                return Ok((Expr::Binary { op: ir_op, left: Box::new(l), right: Box::new(r) }, result));
   610	            }
   611	            other => return Err(unknown(site, format!("unknown operator {other}"), "use =, !=, <, <=, >, >=, +, -, *, and, or, ??")),
   612	        };
   613	        let mut present = Vec::new();
   614	        if matches!(ir_op, BinaryOp::Lt | BinaryOp::Lte | BinaryOp::Gt | BinaryOp::Gte) {
   615	            if nullable_left { present.push(l.clone()); }
   616	            if nullable_right { present.push(r.clone()); }
   617	        }
   618	        let mut comparison = Expr::Binary { op: ir_op, left: Box::new(l), right: Box::new(r) };
   619	        // @ref LLP 3000.013#2.1 — predicate nulls do not enter ordering;
   620	        // the ordinary interpreter's total value ordering remains unchanged.
   621	        for value in present.into_iter().rev() {
   622	            comparison = Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::And,
   623	                left: Box::new(Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::Ne, left: Box::new(value), right: Box::new(ir::lit(Value::Null)) }),
   624	                right: Box::new(comparison) };
   625	        }
   626	        Ok((comparison, Ty::Bool))
   627	    }
   628	
   629	    /// An expression in an identity position: a text literal becomes an id.
   630	    pub(super) fn expr_as_identity(&mut self, expr: &A, out: &mut setup::Body, expected: &Ty) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
   631	        if let A::Literal { value: Literal::Str(text), .. } = expr {
   632	            if text.is_empty() {
   633	                return Err(type_error(expr.site(), "an empty text literal cannot be an id", "use a non-empty id literal, or null"));
   634	            }
   635	            return Ok((Expr::Literal(Value::Id(text.clone())), expected.required()));
   636	        }
   637	        self.expr(expr, out)
   638	    }
   639	
   640	    pub(super) fn expr_as_reference(&mut self, expr: &A, out: &mut setup::Body, expected: &Ty) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
   641	        let (value, ty) = self.expr_as_identity(expr, out, expected)?;
   642	        Ok(self.row_identity(value, ty, expected))
   643	    }
   644	
   645	    // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#8 — contextual projection is exactly `.id`,
   646	    // without a lookup; optional and cross-table rows still need an edit.
   647	    pub(super) fn row_identity(&self, value: Expr, ty: Ty, expected: &Ty) -> (Expr, Ty) {
   648	        if !ty.is_optional() && matches!(ty.required(), Ty::Row(_) | Ty::WriteRow(_)) {
   649	            let table = match ty.required() { Ty::Row(t) | Ty::WriteRow(t) => t, _ => unreachable!() };
   650	            if expected.required() == Ty::Ref(table.clone()) {
   651	                return (ir::field(value, "id"), Ty::Ref(table));
   652	            }
   653	        }
   654	        (value, ty)
   655	    }
   656	
   657	    pub(super) fn call(&mut self, name: &str, args: &[A], site: &Site, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
   658	        if let Some(result) = self.job_query_call(name, args, site, out) { return result; }
   659	        // Compiler-only references bypass the function catalog entirely.
   660	        let primitive = name.strip_prefix("$builtin:");
   661	        if primitive.is_none() && let Some(function) = self.catalog.functions.get(name).cloned() {
   662	            return self.fn_call(&function, args, site, out);
   663	        }
   664	        let name = primitive.unwrap_or(name);
   665	        let arity = |n: usize, rewrite: &str| -> Fallible<()> {
   666	            if args.len() != n {
   667	                return Err(type_error(site, format!("{name} takes {n} argument{}; received {}", if n == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, args.len()), rewrite));
   668	            }
   669	            Ok(())
   670	        };
   671	        match name {
   672	            "receiptSettled" if primitive.is_some() => {
   673	                arity(1, "receipt settlement needs a row")?;
   674	                let (value, ty) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
   675	                let Ty::Row(table) = ty else { return Err(type_error(site, "receipt settlement needs a row", "use a receipt row")); };
   676	                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::ReceiptSettled { table }, args: vec![value] }, Ty::Bool))
   677	            }
   678	            super::super::intent_variants::PRESENT => {
   679	                let (value, _) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
   680	                Ok((Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::Ne, left: Box::new(value), right: Box::new(Expr::Literal(Value::Null)) }, Ty::Bool))
   681	            }
   682	            super::super::intent_variants::SEARCH => {
   683	                let (value, ty) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
   684	                if !matches!(ty, Ty::Text(_)) { return Err(type_error(site, "matching needs present text", "matching (q ?? '')")); }
   685	                let A::Name { name, .. } = &args[1] else { unreachable!("planned needle binding") };
   686	                let runtime = self.temp("intentNeedle");
   687	                self.declare(name, ty);
   688	                self.scopes.last_mut().unwrap().get_mut(name).unwrap().runtime = runtime.clone();
   689	                out.push(Stmt::Let { name: runtime.clone(), value });
   690	                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::SearchPresent, args: vec![ir::var(&runtime)] }, Ty::Bool))
   691	            }
   692	            "day" | "hour" | "bucket" => {
   693	                let (millis, offset) = super::super::maintains::calendar(name, args, site)?;
   694	                let (value, ty) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
   695	                if ty != Ty::Time { return Err(type_error(args[0].site(), format!("{name} needs a required time, got {}", ty.name()), "pass a required time column or now")); }
   696	                let mut args = vec![value];
   697	                if offset != 0 { args.push(Expr::Literal(Value::Int(offset))); }
   698	                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Calendar { millis }, args }, Ty::Int))
   699	            }
   700	            // @ref LLP 3000.040#22-builtins — months since 1970-01 and calendar years, UTC, and back to a time.
   701	            "month" | "year" => {
   702	                arity(1, &format!("{name}(time); civil periods are UTC and take no offset"))?;
   703	                let (value, ty) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
   704	                if ty != Ty::Time { return Err(type_error(args[0].site(), format!("{name} needs a required time, got {}", ty.name()), format!("{name}(.at), {name}(now), or {name}(t ?? now)")).guide("time")); }
   705	                let function = if name == "month" { Civil::Month } else { Civil::Year };
   706	                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Civil(function), args: vec![value] }, Ty::Int))
   707	            }
   708	            "monthStart" | "yearStart" => {
   709	                let unit = if name == "monthStart" { "month" } else { "year" };
   710	                arity(1, &format!("{name}({unit}); {unit}(t) gives one"))?;
   711	                let (value, ty) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
   712	                if ty != Ty::Int { return Err(type_error(args[0].site(), format!("{name} takes a {unit} number (an int), got {}", ty.name()), format!("{name}({unit}(t)), or {name}({unit}(now) + 1) for the next")).guide("time")); }
   713	                let function = if name == "monthStart" { Civil::MonthStart } else { Civil::YearStart };
   714	                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Civil(function), args: vec![value] }, Ty::Time))
   715	            }
   716	            "count" => {
   717	                arity(1, "count(list)")?;
   718	                if let Some(read) = self.aggregate_domain(&args[0]) && self.is_page(&read, ReadMode::FilteredPoint)? {
   719	                    let saved = self.total.replace(("count", None));
   720	                    let scanned = self.scan_at(&read, out, prefix::Position::Aggregate);
   721	                    self.total = saved;
   722	                    let (scan, _) = scanned?;
   723	                    self.shape_meter_note(&scan, &read);
   724	                    return Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Count, args: vec![Expr::Scan(scan)] }, Ty::Int));
   725	                }
   726	                let (e, t) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
   727	                if matches!(t, Ty::Text(_)) {
   728	                    return Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Len, args: vec![e] }, Ty::Int));
   729	                }
   730	                if t.loop_max().is_none() {
   731	                    return Err(type_error(
   732	                        args[0].site(),
   733	                        format!("count takes present text, a list or a page, got {}", t.name()),
   734	                        "count(text), count(list), or count(page); narrow optional values first",
   735	                    ));
   736	                }
   737	                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Count, args: vec![e] }, Ty::Int))
   738	            }
   739	            "lower" | "trim" => {
   740	                arity(1, &format!("{name}(text)"))?;
   741	                let (value, ty) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
   742	                let Ty::Text(max) = ty else {
   743	                    return Err(type_error(site, format!("{name} takes present text, got {}", ty.name()), &format!("{name}(text ?? '')")));
   744	                };
   745	                let (builtin, max) = if name == "lower" { (Builtin::Lower, max.saturating_mul(3)) } else { (Builtin::Trim, max) };
   746	                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin, args: vec![value] }, Ty::Text(max)))
   747	            }
   748	            "sha256" => {
   749	                arity(1, "sha256(text)")?;
   750	                let (value, ty) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
   751	                if !matches!(ty, Ty::Text(_)) {
   752	                    return Err(type_error(site, format!("sha256 takes present text, got {}", ty.name()), "sha256(text ?? '')"));
   753	                }
   754	                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Sha256, args: vec![value] }, Ty::Text(64)))
   755	            }
   756	            "group" => {
   757	                arity(2, "group(list, 'column')")?;
   758	                let (value, ty) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
   759	                let Some((item, max)) = ty.sequence() else { return Err(type_error(site, "group takes a list or page", "group(rows, 'column')")); };
   760	                let A::Literal { value: Literal::Str(field), .. } = &args[1] else { return Err(type_error(args[1].site(), "group names one field with a text literal", "group(rows, 'column')")); };
   761	                let (selection, key) = self.member(Expr::Literal(Value::Null), item.clone(), field, args[1].site())?;
   762	                let optional = matches!(selection, Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::OptionalField { .. }, .. });
   763	                let group = Ty::Object(BTreeMap::from([("key".into(), key), ("items".into(), Ty::List(Box::new(item), max))]));
   764	                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Group { field: field.clone(), optional }, args: vec![value] }, Ty::List(Box::new(group), max)))
   765	            }
   766	            "first" | "last" | "at" => {
   767	                arity(if name == "at" { 2 } else { 1 }, &format!("{name}(list{})", if name == "at" { ", index" } else { "" }))?;
   768	                let values = self.strict_args(args, out)?;
   769	                let Some((item, _)) = values[0].1.sequence() else { return Err(type_error(args[0].site(), format!("{name} takes a list or page"), &format!("{name}(rows)"))); };
   770	                if name == "at" && values[1].1 != Ty::Int { return Err(type_error(args[1].site(), "at's index is an int", "at(list, 0)")); }
   771	                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: match name { "first" => Builtin::First, "last" => Builtin::Last, _ => Builtin::At }, args: values.into_iter().map(|(value, _)| value).collect() }, item.optional()))
   772	            }
   773	            "join" => {
   774	                arity(2, "join(list, separator)")?;
   775	                let [(list, lt), (sep, st)]: [(Expr, Ty); 2] = self.strict_args(args, out)?.try_into().expect("checked arity");
   776	                let max = match (lt.sequence(), &st) {
   777	                    (Some((item, count)), Ty::Text(sep)) => match item {
   778	                        Ty::Text(max) => max.saturating_mul(count).saturating_add(sep.saturating_mul(count.saturating_sub(1))),
   779	                        Ty::Unknown if count == 0 => 0,
   780	                        _ => return Err(type_error(site, "join takes a list of present text values", "join(['a', 'b'], ', ')")),
   781	                    },
   782	                    _ => return Err(type_error(site, "join takes a list of present text values and a text separator", "join(['a', 'b'], ', ')")),
   783	                };
   784	                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Join, args: vec![list, sep] }, Ty::Text(max)))
   785	            }
   786	            "sum" if args.len() == 2 => {
   787	                let source = if let Some(read) = self.aggregate_domain(&args[0]) {
   788	                    let saved = self.total.replace(("sum", Some(print::expression(&args[1]))));
   789	                    let scanned = self.scan_at(&read, out, prefix::Position::Aggregate);
   790	                    self.total = saved;
   791	                    let (scan, _) = scanned?;
   792	                    self.shape_meter_note(&scan, &read);
   793	                    if scan.take == Bound::Meter {
   794	                        let saved = self.focal.replace(("$filter".into(), Ty::Row(read.table.clone())));
   795	                        let mut setup = setup::Body::default();
   796	                        let predicate_context = std::mem::replace(&mut self.in_predicate, false);
   797	                        let projected = self.expr(&args[1], &mut setup);
   798	                        self.in_predicate = predicate_context;
   799	                        self.focal = saved;
   800	                        let (projection, ty) = projected?;
   801	                        if !ty.is_numeric() || !setup.is_empty() {
   802	                            return Err(type_error(args[1].site(), "a streaming sum needs a required numeric column", "sum(messages[prefix] by index, .amount)"));
   803	                        }
   804	                        return Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Sum, args: vec![Expr::Scan(scan), projection] }, ty));
   805	                    }
   806	                    let ty = Ty::Page(read.table, scan.take.maximum() as u32);
   807	                    (Expr::Scan(scan), ty)
   808	                } else { self.expr(&args[0], out)? };
   809	                // `sum(page, .x)`: the rows' field, summed — a loop that
   810	                // pushes each projection, then the sum of the list.
   811	                let (source, source_ty) = source;
   812	                let (domain, item_ty) = match (&source, &source_ty) {
   813	                    (Expr::Scan(scan), Ty::Page(table, _)) => (LoopDomain::Page(scan.clone()), Ty::Row(table.clone())),
   814	                    (_, Ty::Page(table, max)) => (LoopDomain::DerivedArray { value: source.clone(), max: *max, bound_source: "sum".into() }, Ty::Row(table.clone())),
   815	                    (_, Ty::Collection(item, max)) | (_, Ty::List(item, max)) => (LoopDomain::DerivedArray { value: source.clone(), max: *max, bound_source: "sum".into() }, item.as_ref().clone()),
   816	                    (_, other) => return Err(type_error(args[0].site(), format!("sum takes a page or a bounded list, got {}", other.name()), "sum(t[prefix] first 50 by index, .amount)")),
   817	                };
   818	                let list = self.temp("sum");
   819	                let item = self.temp("row");
   820	                out.push(Stmt::Let { name: list.clone(), value: Expr::Array(Vec::new()) });
   821	                let mut body = setup::Body::default();
   822	                self.push_scope();
   823	                self.declare(&item, item_ty.clone());
   824	                let saved = self.focal.replace((item.clone(), item_ty));
   825	                let projected = self.expr(&args[1], &mut body);
   826	                self.focal = saved;
   827	                self.pop_scope();
   828	                let (projection, projection_ty) = projected?;
   829	                if !projection_ty.is_numeric() {
   830	                    return Err(type_error(
   831	                        args[1].site(),
   832	                        format!("sum adds numbers; .{} is {}", print::expression(&args[1]).trim_start_matches('.'), projection_ty.name()),
   833	                        if projection_ty.required().is_numeric() { format!("{} ?? 0", print::expression(&args[1])) } else { "name a numeric field: sum(page, .amount)".into() },
   834	                    ));
   835	                }
   836	                body.push(Stmt::Push { target: list.clone(), value: projection });
   837	                out.push_for(item, domain, body);
   838	                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Sum, args: vec![ir::var(&list)] }, projection_ty))
   839	            }
   840	            "sum" => {
   841	                arity(1, "sum(list)")?;
   842	                let (e, t) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
   843	                let Some((item, _)) = t.sequence() else { return Err(type_error(args[0].site(), format!("sum takes a list of numbers, got {}", t.name()), "sum(list), or sum(page, .amount)")); };
   844	                if !item.is_numeric() {
   845	                    return Err(type_error(args[0].site(), format!("sum takes numbers, got a list of {}", item.name()), "map the rows to their numeric field first"));
   846	                }
   847	                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Sum, args: vec![e] }, item))
   848	            }
   849	            "divide" => {
   850	                if !matches!(args.len(), 3 | 4) {
   851	                    return Err(type_error(site, format!("divide takes 3 or 4 arguments, got {}", args.len()),
   852	                        "divide(amount, divisor, 'half-even'), or divide(integer, divisor, 2, 'half-even')"));
   853	                }
   854	                let [(dividend, dividend_ty), (divisor, divisor_ty)]: [(Expr, Ty); 2] = self.strict_args(&args[..2], out)?.try_into().expect("checked arity");
   855	                let (scale, result_ty, rounding_arg) = if args.len() == 4 {
   856	                    if dividend_ty != Ty::Int || divisor_ty != Ty::Int {
   857	                        return Err(type_error(site, format!("scaled divide takes a present int numerator and divisor; got {} and {}", dividend_ty.name(), divisor_ty.name()),
   858	                            "narrow optional values first, then divide(integer, divisor, 2, 'half-even')"));
   859	                    }
   860	                    let Some(scale) = literal_int(&args[2]).filter(|scale| (0..=12).contains(scale)) else {
   861	                        return Err(type_error(args[2].site(), "divide's result scale is an integer literal from 0 through 12", "divide(numerator, denominator, 2, 'half-even')"));
   862	                    };

    34	        let implicit_group = mode == ReadMode::FilteredPoint && info.maintained.is_some() && point.index.is_none();
    35	        if implicit_group { point.index = Some("byGroup".into()); }

    37	        super::super::point_key::check(info, &index, read, &keys.iter().map(|(column, _, ty)|
    38	            (column.as_deref(), !ty.is_optional() && *ty != Ty::Unknown)).collect::<Vec<_>>(), false)?;
    39	        if implicit_group { selection = "complete maintained group key".into(); }
    40	        let extra = keys.len() > index.columns.len();
    41	        let mut equalities = Vec::new();
    42	        if extra {
    43	            for (column, value, ty) in &mut keys {
    44	                let column = column.as_ref().expect("named key");
    45	                if column != "id" && !info.columns.contains_key(column) {
    46	                    return Err(unknown(&read.site, format!("{} has no column {column}", read.table), name_rewrite(column, info.columns.keys().map(String::as_str).chain(["id"]), None)));
    47	                }
    48	                let expected = self.key_ty(info, &index, column);
    49	                if !ty.comparable(&expected) { return Err(type_error(&read.site, format!("{column} is {}; {}.{column} is {}", ty.name(), read.table, expected.name()), format!("use {} for {column}", expected.name()))); }

    51	                if !index.columns.contains(column) { equalities.push((column.clone(), value.clone())); }
    52	            }
    53	            keys.retain(|(column, _, _)| index.columns.contains(column.as_ref().unwrap()));
    54	        }

    58	        self.sources.insert(location.clone(), (read.site.clone(), print::read_expr(read)));

    61	        if mode == ReadMode::Exists && equalities.is_empty() {

    63	        }
    64	        if equalities.is_empty() { return Ok(if mode == ReadMode::Exists { Expr::Exists(point) } else { Expr::Get(point) }); }
