    82	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.3 — a seek constrains the first index column after the pinned prefix.
    83	    pub(super) fn seek(&mut self, info: &'a TableInfo, read: &ReadExpr, index: &ast::IndexDecl, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<Option<ir::Range>> {
    84	        if read.seeks.is_empty() { return Ok(None); }
    85	        let mut range = ir::Range { gt: None, gte: None, lt: None, lte: None };
    86	        for bound in &read.seeks {
    87	            if index.columns.get(read.keys.len()) != Some(&bound.column) || read.matching.is_some() {
    88	                return Err(type_error(&bound.site, "a seek compares the first unpinned column of a plain index", "t[prefix, col >= start, col < end] first 50 by index"));
    89	            }
    90	            let expected = self.key_ty(info, index, &bound.column);
    91	            let (value, ty) = self.field_value(&ObjectField { spread: false, name: bound.column.clone(), value: Some(bound.value.clone()), site: bound.site.clone() }, &expected, out)?;
    92	            if !ty.comparable(&expected) || ty.is_optional() {
    93	                let endpoint = print::expression(&bound.value);
    94	                let rewrite = if ty.is_optional() {
    95	                    format!("put the read inside `if {endpoint} != null:`, then `{} where .{} {} {endpoint}`", read.table, bound.column, bound.op)
    96	                } else {
    97	                    format!("use a present {} endpoint in `{} where .{} {} {endpoint}`", expected.required().name(), read.table, bound.column, bound.op)
    98	                };
    99	                return Err(type_error(&bound.site, format!("seek on {}.{} expects present {}, got {}", read.table, bound.column, expected.required().name(), ty.name()), rewrite));
   100	            }
   101	            let slot = match bound.op.as_str() { ">" => &mut range.gt, ">=" => &mut range.gte, "<" => &mut range.lt, "<=" => &mut range.lte, _ => unreachable!("parser seek comparison") };
   102	            if slot.is_some() { return Err(type_error(&bound.site, "a seek bound is repeated", "write one lower and one upper bound")); }
   103	            *slot = Some(Box::new(self.snapshot(value, out)));
   104	        }
   105	        if (range.gt.is_some() && range.gte.is_some()) || (range.lt.is_some() && range.lte.is_some()) {
   106	            return Err(type_error(&read.site, "a seek has at most one lower and one upper bound", "t[prefix, col >= start, col < end] first 50 by index"));
   107	        }
   108	        // Null sorts below every present value. An upper-only nullable seek
   109	        // must skip the entire null segment, including its id suffixes.
   110	        if range.gt.is_none() && range.gte.is_none()
   111	            && read.seeks.first().is_some_and(|bound| self.key_ty(info, index, &bound.column).is_optional()) {
   112	            range.gt = Some(Box::new(ir::lit(Value::Null)));
   113	        }
   114	        Ok(Some(range))
   115	    }
   116	}

   144	    pub(super) fn scan_filter(&mut self, read: &ReadExpr, index: &ast::IndexDecl) -> Fallible<(ReadExpr, Option<Box<Expr>>)> {
   145	        let mut read = read.clone();
   146	        let Some(mut predicate) = read.filter.take() else { return Ok((read, None)); };
   147	        // Planning knows parameter declarations; binding also knows helper,
   148	        // local and lane selectors. Only present, infallible endpoints may
   149	        // leave the short-circuit predicate in either pass.
   150	        let required = self.scopes.iter().flat_map(|scope| scope.keys())
   151	            .filter(|name| self.binding(name).is_some_and(|binding| !binding.ty.is_optional()))
   152	            .cloned().collect();
   153	        if !read.order_keys.is_empty() && read.matching.is_none() {
   154	            let info = self.table(&read.table, &read.site)?;
   155	            let mut parts = Vec::new(); super::super::intent::split(*predicate, &mut parts);
   156	            let mut residual = Vec::new();
   157	            for part in parts {
   158	                let candidate = super::super::intent::comparison(&part).map(|(column, op, value)| (column, vec![op], value))
   159	                    .or_else(|| super::super::intent::equality(&part, info)
   160	                        .filter(|(column, _)| !self.key_ty(info, index, column).is_optional())
   161	                        .map(|(column, value)| (column, vec![">=".into(), "<=".into()], value)));
   162	                if let Some((column, ops, value)) = candidate
   163	                    && index.columns.get(read.keys.len()) == Some(&column)
   164	                    && super::super::intent_aggregates::safe_endpoint(&value, &required)
   165	                    && ops.iter().all(|op| !read.seeks.iter().any(|bound| bound.op.starts_with('<') == op.starts_with('<'))) {
   166	                    for op in ops { read.seeks.push(ast::SeekBound { column: column.clone(), op, value: value.clone(), site: part.site().clone() }); }
   167	                } else { residual.push(part); }
   168	            }
   169	            let Some(remaining) = super::super::intent::conjunction(residual) else { return Ok((read, None)); };
   170	            predicate = remaining;
   171	        }
   172	        // A single next-column comparison is the same seek as its key spelling.
   173	        if read.seeks.is_empty() && read.matching.is_none()
   174	            && let A::Binary { op, left, right, site } = predicate.as_ref()
   175	            && matches!(op.as_str(), ">" | ">=" | "<" | "<=")
   176	            && let A::Member { base, name, .. } = left.as_ref()
   177	            && matches!(base.as_ref(), A::Focal { .. })
   178	            && index.columns.get(read.keys.len()) == Some(name)
   179	            && !has_focal(right)
   180	            && super::super::intent_aggregates::safe_endpoint(right, &required)
   181	        {
   182	            read.seeks.push(ast::SeekBound { column: name.clone(), op: op.clone(), value: *right.clone(), site: site.clone() });
   183	            self.notes.push(Diagnostic::new(site, "N_SEEK", "a `where` on the next index column is a seek; write it in the key", print::read_expr(&read)).guide("reads"));

   185	        }
   186	        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.3 — an unscoped filter can spend the whole page meter on unrelated authors.
   187	        if self.kind == ProgramKind::Query && read.keys.is_empty() && read.seeks.is_empty() && read.matching.is_none()
   188	            && crate::bind::unique_bound::group_bound(self.schema, &read.table, &[]).is_none_or(|n| n > 128)
   189	            && has_focal(&predicate) && !pins_leading_column(&predicate, index.columns.first().map(String::as_str))
   190	        {
   191	            let info = self.table(&read.table, &read.site)?;
   192	            let follows = follow_edge_filter(&predicate, info);
   193	            let consequence = if follows {
   194	                "pages come back short and incomplete when followed authors are sparse (`complete: false`)"
   195	            } else { "sparse matches can exhaust the row meter and return short `complete: false` pages" };
   196	            // @ref LLP 3000.036#12 — wave 2 (024): a `where` every row passes is the trivial repair.
   197	            let rewrite = match always_true(&predicate, info) {
   198	                Some(column) => format!("drop this `where`: .{column} is required, so every row passes it"),
   199	                None if follows => "pin a column with `where .col = value`, choose `by .col`, or read a `view` (see `snapback4 guide feeds`)".to_owned(),
   200	                None => "pin a column with `where .col = value`, choose `by .col`, read a `view` for a count or total, or drop a `where` every row passes".to_owned(),
   201	            };
   202	            self.notes.push(Diagnostic::new(predicate.site(), "N_SPARSE_FILTER",
   203	                format!("{} by {}: this unscoped `where` pins no index prefix; {consequence}", read.table, index.name),
   204	                rewrite).guide(if follows { "feeds" } else { "reads" }));
   205	        }
   206	        let value = self.row_predicate(&read.table, &predicate)?;
   207	        Ok((read, Some(Box::new(value))))

   210	    pub(super) fn row_predicate(&mut self, table: &str, predicate: &A) -> Fallible<Expr> {
   211	        let row_ty = Ty::Row(table.into());
   212	        let prior = self.focal.replace(("$filter".into(), row_ty.clone()));
   213	        let kind = std::mem::replace(&mut self.kind, ProgramKind::Query);
   214	        let predicate_context = std::mem::replace(&mut self.in_predicate, true);
   215	        let mut body = setup::Body::default();
   216	        self.push_scope();
   217	        // A fresh lexical row snapshot lets short-circuit guards narrow its
   218	        // fields without leaking facts to another scan or an enclosing row.
   219	        self.scopes.last_mut().unwrap().insert("$filter".into(), Binding {
   220	            runtime: "$filter".into(), declared: row_ty.clone(), ty: row_ty,
   221	            parameter: false, revision: 0, fields: BTreeMap::new(), error: None, origins: Vec::new(),
   222	        });
   223	        let bound = self.expr(predicate, &mut body);
   224	        self.pop_scope();
   225	        self.kind = kind;
   226	        self.in_predicate = predicate_context;
   227	        self.focal = prior;
   228	        let (value, ty) = bound?;
   229	        if !ty.is_bool() { return Err(type_error(predicate.site(), format!("where needs a bool predicate, got {}", ty.name()), "where .col = value")); }
   230	        // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.6 — predicate setup, including lazy reads, runs afresh for each rule-visible row.

# Wave 12 language-lane status

Updated: 2026-10-15

## Scope

This lane owns the five semantic gaps: ungrouped maintained totals, sound
aggregate and maintained-result narrowing, email text format, enum search,
and exact rounded decimal division. It does not own engine expiry,
`maintained_id`, parser recovery, reserved-name diagnostics or the branch
planner.

## Progress

- Governing LLPs, guide cards, wave evidence lanes 019/021/027/083/091/093,
  NA10 and the pattern ledger read.
- Baseline gate `/tmp/lang-baseline-ready` observed before production edits.
- LLP 3000.013.001 records the semantic and verification contract and is
  linked into `llp/current/`.
- Email schema/runtime/client support landed in `b081f96054`.
- The remaining semantic foundation landed in `0fe7cc1263`: ungrouped global
  maintained counts, enum search, exact three/four-argument rounded division,
  and capture-time count provenance with stale-proof invalidation.
- Cross-runtime evidence landed in `4156cdf7e5`: generated rounded-division
  cases cover every mode/scale and compile into the Lean fragment; one drawn
  representative executes through native, Lean and both device stores.
  Simulator and device scenarios exercise all five surfaces; standalone Lean witnesses
  cover the semantic fragments outside the row evaluator.
- The shared Lean lowering compile blocker reported in the coordination inbox
  is repaired; both Wave 12 language test executables compile again.
- Affected language tests pass 6/6. Simulator, difftest generation, memory
  device and SQLite device tests pass 1/1 each. Lean passes 54 build jobs, 65
  audited theorems, 88/88 examples and 7/7 fixtures. The focused CLI guide
  lookup regression passes, and `ref-check --verbose` passes.
- The full guide test currently passes 120/123. Its three residual failures
  are in concurrent, uncommitted diagnostics documentation: the maintained
  disclosure example names an undeclared table and exceeds its card budget,
  a personas block duplicates the project identity declaration, and their
  added prose moves the corpus-wide reduction ratio. Wave 12's modified guide
  examples, compiled-block preservation, language execution and email
  expectation all pass in that same run.
- The first blind pair found stale count recapture, global page
  misclassification and an email diagnostic-code mismatch; `108c2aeeab`
  closes those counterexamples. The second pair found that the global scalar
  still entered loop/aggregate domains and that one IR assertion was stale.
  The fixes now reject loop, aggregate and `exists` use, assert the actual
  point-read IR, and pass `maintains` 15/15 plus Wave 12 semantics 6/6. A fresh
  same-revision review pair remains in progress.

## Concerns / decisions

- Count non-emptiness is an exact transaction fact, never a general theorem
  prover; conservative misses are acceptable, stale acceptance is not.
- The intermediate census's owner-or-manager structural-fanout refusals are
  in the planner/diagnostics lanes: this lane does not change OR-role planning.
- Hidden maintained misses remain null. Zero is produced only after an
  authorization proof.
- Rounded division uses exact signed integer quotient/remainder and an
  explicit enum mode. The four-argument integer form also names result scale,
  so fractional averages need no manual fixed-point multiply; no floating
  point or implicit `avg` is introduced.

    15	impl Binder<'_> {
    16	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.2 — a repeated pure call narrows like a snapshot field.
    17	    // Facts live on *every* argument root so the existing branch intersections,
    18	    // reassignment invalidation and loop fixed point apply to them as to fields.
    19	    fn stable_call(&self, value: &A) -> Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)> {
    20	        if !matches!(value, A::Call { .. }) { return None; }
    21	        let mut roots = BTreeSet::new();
    22	        let stable = self.stable_value(value, &mut roots)?;
    23	        if roots.is_empty() { roots.insert(CONSTANTS.into()); }
    24	        Some((vec!["$pureCall".into(), stable.key()], roots))
    25	    }
    26	
    27	    pub(super) fn stable_value(&self, value: &A, roots: &mut BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<Stable> {
    28	        match value {
    29	            A::Literal { .. } => Some(Stable::Literal(print::expression(value))),
    30	            A::Name { name, .. } if name == "viewer" => Some(Stable::Viewer),
    31	            A::Name { name, .. } if matches!(name.as_str(), "now" | "commit" | "new") => None,
    32	            A::Name { .. } | A::Member { .. } | A::Focal { .. } => {
    33	                let (root, path) = control::field_path(value, self.focal.as_ref().map(|(name, _)| name.as_str()))?;
    34	                let runtime = if let Some(binding) = self.binding(&root) {
    35	                    roots.insert(root.clone());
    36	                    binding.runtime.clone()
    37	                } else {
    38	                    // A shape's implicit row is an immutable lexical snapshot.
    39	                    // Its unique runtime identity separates projection scopes;
    40	                    // with no mutable argument roots, use the constant anchor.
    41	                    self.focal.as_ref().filter(|(name, _)| name == &root)?.0.clone()
    42	                };
    43	                Some(Stable::Snapshot(runtime, path))
    44	            }
    45	            A::Call { name, args, .. } => {
    46	                let function = self.catalog.functions.get(name)?;
    47	                if !self.pure_functions.get(&function.name).copied().unwrap_or(false) { return None; }
    48	                Some(Stable::Call(function.name.clone(), args.iter().map(|arg| self.stable_value(arg, roots)).collect::<Option<_>>()?))
    49	            }
    50	            _ => None,
    51	        }
    52	    }

    54	    pub(super) fn narrow_call(&mut self, value: &A, present: bool) {
    55	        let Some((key, roots)) = self.stable_call(value) else { return; };
    56	        let Some(ty) = self.call_types.get(&key) else { return; };
    57	        let ty = if present { ty.required() } else { Ty::Null };
    58	        for root in roots {
    59	            let mut binding = self.binding(&root).expect("a stable root").clone();
    60	            binding.fields.insert(key.clone(), ty.clone());
    61	            self.scopes.last_mut().expect("a scope").insert(root, binding);
    62	        }
    63	    }
    64	
    65	    pub(super) fn record_call(&mut self, value: &A, ty: &Ty) {
    66	        if let Some((key, _)) = self.stable_call(value) { self.call_types.insert(key, ty.clone()); }
    67	    }

    69	    pub(super) fn call_refinement(&self, value: &A) -> Option<Ty> {
    70	        let (key, roots) = self.stable_call(value)?;
    71	        let mut result = None;
    72	        for root in roots {
    73	            let ty = self.binding(&root)?.fields.get(&key)?;
    74	            if result.as_ref().is_some_and(|other| other != ty) { return None; }
    75	            result = Some(ty.clone());
    76	        }
    77	        result
    78	    }

   108	        Expr::Block { body, value } => statements(body) && expression(value),
   109	    }
   110	}
   111	
   112	fn builtin_pure(builtin: &Builtin) -> bool {
   113	    match builtin {
   114	        Builtin::RequireUncapped => false,
   115	        Builtin::JobAs | Builtin::JobQuery { .. } => false,
   116	        Builtin::Connected | Builtin::ReceiptSettled { .. } => false,
   117	        Builtin::ProjectFields { .. } | Builtin::OptionalField { .. } | Builtin::Calendar { .. } | Builtin::Civil(_)
   118	        | Builtin::Len | Builtin::Slice | Builtin::Concat | Builtin::Lower | Builtin::Trim

   120	        | Builtin::At | Builtin::Min | Builtin::Max | Builtin::Extremum { .. }
   121	        | Builtin::ExtremumOf { .. } | Builtin::Divmod { .. } | Builtin::Divide { .. } | Builtin::Sort { .. }
   122	        | Builtin::MentionTokens | Builtin::SearchPresent | Builtin::DeterministicShare
   123	        | Builtin::Count | Builtin::Sum | Builtin::CountCapped => true,
   124	    }

   106	fn int_range(kind: &ColumnType) -> bool {
   107	    match kind {
   108	        ColumnType::IntRange { .. } => true,
   109	        ColumnType::Optional(inner) | ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => int_range(inner),
   110	        _ => false,
   111	    }
   112	}
   113	
   114	fn ordered_units(table: &Table, rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   115	    let units = |term: &RuleTerm| matches!(term, RuleTerm::Field(f) if matches!(table.columns.get(f), Some(ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. })));
   116	    match rule {
   117	        RuleExpr::Compare(_, l, r) => units(l) || units(r),
   118	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| ordered_units(table, item)),
   119	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered_units(table, inner),
   120	        _ => false,
   121	    }
   122	}
   123	
   124	fn ordered(rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   125	    match rule {
   126	        RuleExpr::Compare(..) => true,
   127	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(ordered),
   128	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered(inner),
   129	        _ => false,
   130	    }
   131	}

   146	        let required = self.required_capabilities();

   148	        // ordinary schemas, including the serialized conformance corpus.
   149	        if required.is_empty() { return Wire::serialize(self, serializer); }
   150	        let mut wire = self.clone();
   151	        for table in wire.tables.values_mut() {
   152	            table.constraints.retain(|c| !matches!(c, Constraint::Recorded));
   153	        }
   154	        let mut carrier = wire.tables.first_entry().ok_or_else(||
   155	            serde::ser::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: required capabilities need a table carrier"))?;
   156	        carrier.get_mut().constraints.push(Constraint::Capabilities(required));
   157	        Wire::serialize(&wire, serializer)
   158	    }
   159	}

   145	fn aggregate_identity_capability_upgrades_legacy_wire_and_fences_old_devices() {
   146	    let schema = compile("table entries:\n  group: text <=64\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .group\n  public\n");
   147	    assert!(schema.required_capabilities().contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"));
   148	
   149	    // A pre-migration stored schema may already have a carrier for unrelated
   150	    // capabilities. Decode it once, then stamp the digest identity capability
   151	    // on every newly published schema/projection.
   152	    let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&schema).unwrap();
   153	    for table in legacy["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
   154	        for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
   155	            if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
   156	                names.retain(|value| value != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
   157	            }
   158	        }
   159	    }
   160	    let upgraded: Schema = serde_json::from_value(legacy).unwrap();
   161	    let encoded = serde_json::to_string(&upgraded).unwrap();

   164	    let required = snapback4_core::device_protocol::compatibility(&upgraded.public_projection());
   165	    let mut old = snapback4_core::device_protocol::DeviceEngine::current();
   166	    old.version = "0.4.28".into();
   167	    old.capabilities.retain(|capability| capability != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
   168	    let refusal = snapback4_core::device_protocol::check(Some(&old), &required).unwrap_err();
   169	    assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_DEVICE_VERSION");

     9	// Each adapter is compared with the entry point it replaced, not another funnel.
    10	fn same_decode<T: std::fmt::Debug>(old: Result<T, serde_json::Error>, new: Result<T, serde_json::Error>, positions: bool) {
    11	    match (old, new) {
    12	        (Ok(old), Ok(new)) => assert_eq!(format!("{old:?}"), format!("{new:?}")),
    13	        (Err(old), Err(new)) => {
    14	            assert_eq!(old.to_string(), new.to_string());
    15	            if positions { assert_eq!((old.line(), old.column()), (new.line(), new.column())); }
    16	        }
    17	        (old, new) => panic!("baseline/funnel disagree: {old:?} / {new:?}"),
    18	    }
    19	}

    21	fn decode<T: DeserializeOwned + std::fmt::Debug>(text: &str) {
    22	    same_decode(serde_json::from_str::<T>(text), codec::from_text::<T>(text), true);
    23	    same_decode(serde_json::from_slice::<T>(text.as_bytes()), codec::from_slice::<T>(text.as_bytes()), true);
    24	    if let Ok(tree) = serde_json::from_str::<Json>(text) {
    25	        same_decode(serde_json::from_value::<T>(tree.clone()), codec::from_value::<T>(tree), true);
    26	    }
    27	}
    28	
    29	fn encode<T: Serialize>(value: &T) {
    30	    same_decode(serde_json::to_string(value), codec::to_text(value), true);
    31	    same_decode(serde_json::to_value(value), codec::to_value(value), true);
    32	    same_decode(serde_json::to_vec(value), codec::to_vec(value), true);
    33	}

    45	// Borrow the real store so a refused opening leaves it available for inspection.
    46	struct Borrowed<'a, S>(&'a mut S);
    47	impl<S: DeviceStore> DeviceStore for Borrowed<'_, S> {
    48	    type Tx<'a> = S::Tx<'a> where Self: 'a;
    49	    fn install(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    50	        self.0.install(schema, metadata, reset)
    51	    }
    52	    fn install_checked(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool, expected: &BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    53	        self.0.install_checked(schema, metadata, reset, expected)
    54	    }
    55	    fn meta(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> { self.0.meta(key) }
    56	    fn set_meta(&mut self, key: &str, value: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> { self.0.set_meta(key, value) }
    57	    fn transaction(&mut self) -> Result<Self::Tx<'_>, RuntimeError> { self.0.transaction() }
    58	}

    60	fn refused_reopen_preserves<S: DeviceStore>(store: &mut S) {
    61	    let backend = plain();
    62	    drop(Device::open_store(Borrowed(store), Some(backend.clone())).unwrap());
    63	    let row = object([("id", Value::Id("kept".into()))]);
    64	    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
    65	    tx.put("t", &backend.schema.tables["t"], &row, None).unwrap();
    66	    tx.commit().unwrap();
    67	    let mut future = serde_json::to_value(&backend).unwrap();
    68	    future["schema"]["tables"]["t"]["constraints"] = json!([{"Capabilities":["future-derivation"]}]);
    69	    store.set_meta("device:backend", &future.to_string()).unwrap();
    70	    let mut replacement = backend;
    71	    replacement.generation = 2; // Without the fence this resets the held row.
    72	    let before = store.transaction().unwrap().meta_prefix("").unwrap();
    73	    for opening in [Opening::Install(replacement.clone()), Opening::Kept, Opening::Initial(replacement)] {
    74	        let error = match opening.open(Borrowed(store)) {
    75	            Err(error) => error,
    76	            Ok(_) => panic!("unsupported kept backend accepted during reopening"),
    77	        };
    78	        assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY");
    79	        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
    80	        assert_eq!(tx.meta_prefix("").unwrap(), before, "refusal must preserve all metadata");
    81	        assert_eq!(tx.get("t", "kept").unwrap(), Some(row.clone()), "refusal must preserve rows");
    82	    }
    83	}

   102	// Linux counterpart of schema-capabilities.test.mjs's published-engine fence.
   103	// Include DDL (indexes/triggers/columns), every table and every stored value.
   104	// The refusal contract covers schema/rows, integrity and freelist count.
   105	// WAL identity is asserted for the small no-spill cases below; a large rolled
   106	// back migration may change free-page contents or retain uncommitted frames
   107	// (LLP 3000.033 §1.3).
   108	fn sqlite_dump(path: &std::path::Path) -> Vec<(String, Vec<String>)> {
   109	    let db = rusqlite::Connection::open_with_flags(path, rusqlite::OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY).unwrap();
   110	    let mut tables = vec!["sqlite_schema".to_string()];
   111	    tables.extend(db.prepare("SELECT name FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'table' ORDER BY name").unwrap()
   112	        .query_map([], |r| r.get::<_, String>(0)).unwrap().map(Result::unwrap));
   113	    let mut snapshot = tables.into_iter().map(|name| {
   114	        let mut stmt = db.prepare(&format!("SELECT * FROM \"{}\"", name.replace('"', "\"\""))).unwrap();
   115	        let columns = stmt.column_count();
   116	        let mut rows = stmt.query_map([], |r| (0..columns).map(|i| r.get::<_, rusqlite::types::Value>(i)).collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<_>>>())
   117	            .unwrap().map(|r| format!("{:?}", r.unwrap())).collect::<Vec<_>>();
   118	        rows.sort();
   119	        (name, rows)
   120	    }).collect::<Vec<_>>();
   121	    let integrity: String = db.query_row("PRAGMA integrity_check", [], |r| r.get(0)).unwrap();
   122	    assert_eq!(integrity, "ok");
   123	    let free: i64 = db.query_row("PRAGMA freelist_count", [], |r| r.get(0)).unwrap();
   124	    snapshot.push(("PRAGMA integrity_check/freelist_count".into(), vec![integrity, free.to_string()]));
   125	    snapshot
   126	}

   128	fn legacy_device(path: &std::path::Path, mode: &str) {
   129	    drop(snapback4_device::native::Device::open(path, Some(plain())).unwrap());
   130	    let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(path).unwrap();
   131	    db.execute("INSERT INTO r(t,id,data) SELECT num,'kept',?1 FROM _catalog WHERE name = 't'",
   132	        [serde_json::to_string(&object([("id", Value::Id("kept".into()))])).unwrap()]).unwrap();
   133	    db.execute_batch("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _read_sessions;").unwrap();
   134	    let has_scope: bool = db.query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pragma_table_info('_session_mint_bindings') WHERE name = 'scope')", [], |r| r.get(0)).unwrap();
   135	    if has_scope { db.execute_batch("ALTER TABLE _session_mint_bindings DROP COLUMN scope;").unwrap(); }
   136	    db.execute_batch(&format!("PRAGMA journal_mode = {mode};")).unwrap();
   137	}

     1	# Device engine handshake and build identity
     2	
     3	**Type:** RFC
     4	**Status:** Draft
     5	**Systems:** snapback4, wire, devices, CLI, workers
     6	**Author:** Charlie Cheever (implementation by Codex)
     7	**Date:** 2026-10-12
     8	**Revised:** 2026-10-14 (NARR stamp diagnostics); 2026-10-14 (EXPOFIX); 2026-10-13
     9	**Related:** [LLP 3000.001](./3000.001-durable-replica-and-write-lifecycle.research.md), [LLP 3000](./3000-snapback4.explainer.md), [LLP 3000.009 §5.3](./3000.009-general-purpose-backend.rfc.md#5.3), [LLP 3000.000.000](./3000.000.000-retained-storage-and-hot-release.rfc.md)
    10	
    11	## Problem
    12	
    13	Wave 9 R1/DT4 found checked-in Exact wasm engines silently lagging npm/server upgrades. Schema capability decoding and missing generation diagnostics arrived too late. R6 found supervised workers resolving packages beside releases outside the app, and simulated dev time expiring their injected tokens.
    14	
    15	## Protocol
    16	
    17	A device engine reports `{format:1, version:"0.4.24", capabilities:[...]}` from Rust. Memory, SQLite, wasm and Expo native share the same source. The client sends this JSON as `x-snapback-device` on every `/sync` and `/changes`, also on `/schema` before opening/adopting any backend. CORS permits the header. Neither a JavaScript package version nor a server echo stands in for device identity. Native and wasm hosts expose `snapback4_device::engine::info()` and `engine::headers()` without opening a store; wrappers forward `engine_info` and `engine_headers` before partition dispatch. Exact's Rust Fetch constructors attach the crate-owned headers and both Rust and TypeScript transport drivers forward them after caller credentials, overriding any caller-supplied device header. An unmodified adapter can obtain it from the opened core but cannot protect initial schema decoding; the paved adapters all supply it before open.
    18	
    19	Authentication precedes compatibility. `/sync` requires the header; an absent, malformed, unsupported-format or too-old engine receives HTTP 409 `{denied:{code:"E_DEVICE_VERSION",family:"device-version",message,...}}` before parsing the sync body or materializing a page. `/schema` and `/changes` check a supplied header; bare one-shot and online-only callers have no replica and need no engine handshake. A legacy device first reaches `/sync` and receives this same refusal instead of an input-field error. No retry drops a modern handshake to bypass the fence.
    20	
    21	The server checks a release's declared minimum version and every schema-required capability plus `sync-generation-v1`. Capabilities are authoritative even for a version above the floor. Version components are unsigned decimal u32 integers on both preflights and the server; overflow or malformed components refuse. Minimum engine version starts at 0.4.24, the first generation-capable union/merged-page release; future semantic releases must raise the constant when existing capabilities cannot represent the change. `GET /` exposes the current public-projection compatibility record for Exact's pre-browser preflight (both dev and serve). Exact compares that floor and capabilities, not npm version equality. Each immutable release writes `device-compatibility.json` with `{server_version,minimum_version,capabilities}`; `/schema` returns the active equivalent as `device_compatibility`. Capabilities come from the public projection, so server-private semantics impose no device requirement. Refusals name device/server versions, the first missing capability (or the floor/handshake), and rebuild commands: Exact `bun exact.mjs snapback --rebuild`, Expo `npx expo run:ios`, web reinstall the server's package version and rebuild the web app. An unversioned legacy device is explicitly `unknown (unstamped)`; its version cannot be inferred honestly.
    22	
    23	The JS local client exports `DeviceVersionError` with a typed incompatible status for initial refusal, and `deviceVersion()` / `onDeviceVersion` for a running client. Runtime sync/poll refusal stops replication, preserves queued writes, and makes affected reads denied. Compatibility is admission, not an authenticity or trust attestation; application servers still enforce every authority rule.
    24	
    25	## Build stamp
    26	
    27	The optimized wasm carries exactly one custom section named `snapback4.engine`, containing canonical UTF-8 JSON in the same engine format: compact JSON, the fields `format`, `version`, `capabilities` in that order, and no other fields. Both stamp readers require reserialization to those exact bytes; duplicate keys, float spellings of format, unknown fields, alternate whitespace/escaping, and invalid UTF-8 refuse. This lexical rule applies to the embedded section, not ordinary transport header JSON. The `snapback4-device` crate generates this from the core's `DeviceEngine::current()` during its build and emits it as a used Rust wasm custom section. Every producer linking the crate inherits it, including Exact's separate wrapper; no packaging script may manufacture or append identity. The package build verifies the section survives bindgen/optimization and matches runtime `engine_info`, then derives a diagnostic `.engine.json` sidecar. The embedded section is authoritative; Exact's `.wasm.json` is also derived diagnostic output and is not read for admission. Native exports `sb4_engine_info`, with JSON freed by `sb4_free`, and the process device exposes `device --engine-info`. Exact's build workstream must copy these wasm bytes intact; its preflight can read the custom section with `WebAssembly.Module.customSections` without instantiating or decoding a backend. Missing, malformed or duplicate sections are unknown and require rebuilding. A stamp is a compatibility statement, not a cryptographic signature.
    28	
    29	`check` and `doctor` inspect app.json in the backend root and immediate child app directories and require `typescript.sources.backend` to resolve to this project's `snapback/generated`. That backend mount only declares generated operations; it does not declare a replica. An Exact device adapter declared in `typescript.sources` as `snapback4/ts` requires `assets/snapback4.wasm`. A relocated adapter is recognized from its runtime import or re-export of `./web.ts` together with that module's runtime import or re-export of `./generated/device.ts`. Named, namespace, default, side-effect, static dynamic imports, import-equals and re-exports are recognized. Erased type-only imports do not establish consumption. Exact's `snapback4/online` adapter and a generated-operations-only mount impose no device gate, even if an unused old default artifact remains on disk.
    30	
    31	Custom artifacts are discovered from static string declarations in app.json, app.ts, and the mounted adapter entry (`snapback.ts`, or a mounted source file). Relative source declarations resolve beside that source; `/assets/` URLs resolve inside the app. Local asset URLs use URL-decoded filenames with query/fragment suffixes removed; an existing literal relative filename takes precedence. Oxc 0.154.0 parses the TypeScript AST in the CLI (without executing source); runtime literal expressions and value module references supply paths. Escapes and templates without substitutions use their decoded values. Comments, regex bodies, erased type/ambient/interface declarations, abstract/declared members, and type-only import/export specifiers do not declare paths. TypeScript declaration files supply no runtime paths. Invalid source is left to Exact's compiler and is not treated as a custom declaration. An identified artifact's missing, malformed, duplicate, noncanonical or incompatible identity refuses check before generated output and marks doctor unhealthy. Unrelated wasm, diagnostic sidecars, comments, and unreferenced artifacts do not declare a device consumer. Computed/remote URLs and declarations solely in transitive secondary modules are outside this static discovery; the runtime handshake still admits the actual device. Apps mounted to another backend are ignored. The Exact tooling and its docs belong to the Exact/DX lanes.

It never issues HTTP refresh successors. Forward advance shifts live expirations before publishing time. Clock reset moves time backwards; old tokens remain unexpired until the same clock-revision replacement stops and revokes them. Store reset retains its ordinary authority semantics.    463	## 4. Fences and compatibility
   464	
   465	| semantics | what an older engine or device does | capability recorded |
   466	|---|---|---|
   467	| `IntRange` in a column | refuses to decode the schema (unknown `ColumnType` tag) | `int-range` |
   468	| `IntRange` in an argument | refuses to decode the program (unknown `ArgType` tag) | — |
   469	| `month`/`year` builtins | refuses to decode the program (unknown `Builtin` tag) | — |
   470	| `month`/`year` calendar keys | refuses `E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: unsupported engine capability calendar-month` (every binary since the capability fence); without the carrier, `CalendarKey::validate` refuses | `calendar-month` |
   471	| monthly schedules | refuses `E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY` naming `calendar-schedule`; without the carrier, admission refuses `every_ms = 0` | `calendar-schedule` |
   472	| whole-table caps | unchanged semantics | — |
   473	
   474	The capabilities are recorded in the schema's carrier, as every new
   475	semantics is. Every binary since the capability fence checks the declared
   476	names after decoding the schema's structure and refuses an unknown one with
   477	`E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY`. So a schema with calendar keys or a calendar schedule
   478	gets the named refusal from an older binary. A schema with an `IntRange`
   479	column fails earlier, in structural decoding (an unknown `ColumnType` tag),
   480	before the capability check is reached; it still fails closed, but with the
   481	decoder's own message. Programs carry no capability: an unknown `ArgType` or
   482	`Builtin` tag refuses the program's decode.
   483	Detection recurses through optional and list columns, index components and
   484	maintain keys.
   485	
   486	Schemas that use none of these features serialize byte for byte as before,
   487	including their schedules, so the conformance corpus, schema hashes,
   488	schedule progress and kept stores are unaffected.
   489

   125	fn calendar<H: Host>(host: &mut H) {
   126	    let (mut server, backend) = compile(SOURCE);

   131	        let on_server = server.query("calendar", context("alice", &[("t", Value::Int(t))]).at(NOW)).unwrap();

   138	    // The extreme starts refuse alike, never a wrong instant.

   140	        let on_server = server.query("starts", context("alice", &[("m", Value::Int(m)), ("y", Value::Int(y))]).at(NOW)).unwrap_err();

   143	    }

   145	    let october = NOW;

   167	fn whole_table_cap<H: Host>(host: &mut H) {
   168	    let (mut server, backend) = compile(SOURCE);
   169	    let mut device = host.open("lang2-cap", Some(backend)).unwrap();
   170	    for (n, page) in snapshot_pages(&mut server, "alice", 10).iter().enumerate() { device.apply(page, n == 0).unwrap(); }
   171	    for (n, name) in ["a", "b", "c"].iter().enumerate() {
   172	        assert_eq!(both::<H>(&mut server, &mut device, "addCategory", json!({"name": name}), &format!("k{n}")), None);
   173	        let watermark = device.state().unwrap().0;
   174	        device.apply(&stream_page(&mut server, "alice", watermark), false).unwrap();
   175	    }
   176	    assert_eq!(both::<H>(&mut server, &mut device, "addCategory", json!({"name": "d"}), "k3").as_deref(), Some("E_CONSTRAINT"));
   177	    let refused = server.mutate("addCategory", None, context("bob", &[("name", Value::String("e".into()))]).at(NOW).with_ids(["k4".to_owned()])).unwrap();
   178	    let WriteState::Failed { why, .. } = refused.state else { panic!("a fourth category was written") };
   179	    assert_eq!(why.message, "categories holds at most 3 rows");
   180	    host.close("lang2-cap", device);
   181	}
   182	
   183	/// Tightening a range over stored rows (LLP 3000.040 §1.6): the server refuses
   184	/// E_ADOPT while a row does not fit and adopts once it is repaired; a device that
   185	/// held the stale image drops it at the new generation and reacquires.
   186	fn tightening<H: Host>(host: &mut H) {
   187	    const LOOSE: &str = "table scores:\n  owner: principal\n  stars: int\n  read <- .owner = viewer\n  insert <- .owner = viewer\n  update <- .owner = viewer\n  sync to .owner\nquery all():\n  return scores where .owner = viewer first 10 by .id\nmutation fix(s: scores, stars: int):\n  update scores[s] { stars }\n  return null\n";
   188	    let (mut server, backend) = compile(LOOSE);
   189	    let table = server.schema().tables["scores"].clone();
   190	    for (id, stars) in [("low", 0), ("ok", 3)] {
   191	        server.seed([("scores".into(), snapback4_core::wire::row_from_json(&table, &json!({"id": id, "owner": "alice", "stars": stars})).unwrap())]).unwrap();
   192	    }
   193	    let mut device = host.open("lang2-tighten", Some(backend)).unwrap();
   194	    for (n, page) in snapshot_pages(&mut server, "alice", 10).iter().enumerate() { device.apply(page, n == 0).unwrap(); }
   195	    let held = device.query("all", "alice", &json!({}), NOW).unwrap().data;
   196	    assert!(snapback4_core::wire::to_json(&held).to_string().contains("\"stars\":0"), "{}", host.label());
   197	    let (_, tight) = compile(&LOOSE.replace("stars: int\n", "stars: int 1..5\n").replace("stars: int):", "stars: int 1..5):"));
   198	    let refused = server.adopt(tight.schema.clone(), tight.programs.clone()).unwrap_err();
   199	    assert_eq!(refused.code(), "E_ADOPT", "{refused}");
   200	    assert!(refused.to_string().contains("int 1..5"), "{refused}");
   201	    assert!(matches!(server.mutate("fix", None, context("alice", &[("s", id("low")), ("stars", Value::Int(1))]).at(NOW)).unwrap().state, WriteState::Sent { .. }));
   202	    server.adopt(tight.schema.clone(), tight.programs.clone()).unwrap();
   203	    let tight = snapback4_device::device::Backend { generation: server.generation(), ..tight };
   204	    device.adopt(tight).unwrap();
   205	    for (n, page) in snapshot_pages(&mut server, "alice", 10).iter().enumerate() { device.apply(page, n == 0).unwrap(); }
   206	    let read = device.query("all", "alice", &json!({}), NOW).unwrap();
   207	    let text = snapback4_core::wire::to_json(&read.data).to_string();
   208	    assert!(!text.contains("\"stars\":0") && text.contains("\"stars\":1"), "{}: {text}", host.label());
   209	    host.close("lang2-tighten", device);
   210	}
   211	
   212	#[test] fn tightening_server_and_memory_device() { tightening(&mut Memory::new()); }
   213	#[test] fn tightening_server_and_sqlite_device() { tightening(&mut Sqlite::new("lang2-tighten")); }
   214	#[test] fn bounded_ints_server_and_memory_device() { bounded(&mut Memory::new()); }
   215	#[test] fn bounded_ints_server_and_sqlite_device() { bounded(&mut Sqlite::new("lang2-bounded")); }
   216	#[test] fn calendar_server_and_memory_device() { calendar(&mut Memory::new()); }
   217	#[test] fn calendar_server_and_sqlite_device() { calendar(&mut Sqlite::new("lang2-calendar")); }
   218	#[test] fn whole_table_cap_server_and_memory_device() { whole_table_cap(&mut Memory::new()); }
   219	#[test] fn whole_table_cap_server_and_sqlite_device() { whole_table_cap(&mut Sqlite::new("lang2-cap")); }

+/// Exact rounded division comes from its own stream, preserving every older
+/// case whose stream does not select the new expression.
+fn rounded_division(case: &mut Case) {
+    let mut rng = Rng::new(case.seed ^ ROUND_DIV_STREAM);
+    if rng.pick(6) != 0 || !matches!(case.program.body, Body::Scalar(_)) { return; }
+    let modes = [Rounding::TowardZero, Rounding::AwayFromZero, Rounding::Floor,
+        Rounding::Ceiling, Rounding::HalfAwayFromZero, Rounding::HalfEven];
+    let dividend = if rng.pick(2) == 0 { Expr::Arg("a".into(), Type::Int) }
+        else { Expr::Int([-7, -5, -1, 0, 1, 5, 7][rng.pick(7) as usize]) };
+    let divisor = if rng.pick(2) == 0 { Expr::Arg("b".into(), Type::Int) }
+        else { Expr::Int([-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3][rng.pick(7) as usize]) };
+    let scale = match rng.pick(5) { 0 => None, 1 => Some(0), 2 => Some(2), 3 => Some(6), _ => Some(12) };
+    case.program.body = Body::Scalar(Expr::RoundedDivide(
+        modes[rng.pick(modes.len() as u64) as usize].clone(), scale, Box::new(dividend), Box::new(divisor)));
+}

+/-- Truncating quotient/remainder followed by one exact rounding step. The
+model deliberately derives truncation from the existing Euclidean primitive,
+so its oracle is independent of the Rust implementation. -/
+def roundedDiv (rounding : Rounding) (scale : Option Nat) (x y : Int) : EM Value := do
+  if y = 0 then refuse "E_DIV_ZERO"
+  let x := x * (10 : Int) ^ scale.getD 0
+  let qe := Int.ediv x y
+  let re := Int.emod x y
+  let q := if x < 0 ∧ re ≠ 0 then qe + (if y < 0 then -1 else 1) else qe
+  let r := x - q * y
+  if r = 0 then checkI53 q else
+    let direction : Int := if (x < 0) = (y < 0) then 1 else -1
+    let away := q + direction
+    let result := match rounding with
+      | .towardZero => q
+      | .awayFromZero => away
+      | .floor => if direction < 0 then away else q
+      | .ceiling => if 0 < direction then away else q
+      | .halfAwayFromZero => if Int.natAbs r * 2 ≥ Int.natAbs y then away else q
+      | .halfEven =>
+          if Int.natAbs r * 2 > Int.natAbs y ∨
+              (Int.natAbs r * 2 = Int.natAbs y ∧ Int.emod q 2 ≠ 0)
+          then away else q
+    checkI53 result
+

   103	    part.all fun c => asciiAlphaNum c || localPunctuation.contains c

   110	def emailValid (email : String) : Bool :=
   111	  let chars := email.toList
   112	  chars.length ≤ 254 && chars.all (·.toNat ≤ 127) &&
   113	    chars.count '@' == 1 && match splitOnce '@' chars with
   114	      | some (localChars, domain) => localPartValid localChars &&

   124	/-- ASCII executable witness for enum spellings using the shared word-search
   125	shape: lowercase, alphanumeric token boundaries, and query-prefix matching.
   126	The Rust/device tests own NFC and the production Unicode tables. -/
   127	def asciiTokens (text : String) : List (List Char) :=
   128	  let rec go (remaining current : List Char) (tokens : List (List Char)) :=
   129	    match remaining with
   130	    | [] => (if current.isEmpty then tokens else current.reverse :: tokens).reverse
   131	    | c :: cs =>
   132	        if asciiAlphaNum c then go cs (asciiLower c :: current) tokens
   133	        else go cs [] (if current.isEmpty then tokens else current.reverse :: tokens)
   134	  go text.toList [] []
   135	
   136	def isPrefix : List Char → List Char → Bool
   137	  | [], _ => true
   138	  | _, [] => false
   139	  | p :: ps, w :: ws => p == w && isPrefix ps ws
   140	
   141	def enumMatchesAscii (value query : String) : Bool :=
   142	  let words := asciiTokens value
   143	  (asciiTokens query).all fun term => words.any fun word => isPrefix term word
   144

   147	example : enumMatchesAscii "museum" "music" = false := by decide

   324	pub(super) fn delta(maintain: &Maintain, source: &Value, direction: i64) -> Result<i128, RuntimeError> {

     3	// field authorization precede result pricing, under the request's one physical
     4	// allowance. 0.4.2's inherited-aggregate, parent-key and event-slot branches
     5	// (LLP 3000.014 §5, LLP 3000.016 §2.2) sit above that boundary and share it.

    10	fn unavailable_aggregate() -> Value { crate::value::object([("value", Value::Null)]) }

    12	impl Runner<'_> {

    14	    // expiry traversal short-circuits. Null points have no witness on any
    15	    // replica; reject before occupancy, coverage or lifetime work. Maintained
    16	    // null groups remain real groups, and population equality is unchanged.
    17	    pub(super) fn null_unique_point(&self, table: &str, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> bool {
    18	        key.contains(&Value::Null) && self.schema.maintain_for(table).is_none()
    19	            && self.schema.table(table).and_then(|t| t.index(index)).is_some_and(|i| i.unique)
    20	    }
    21	
    22	    pub(super) fn created(&self, table: &str, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> bool {
    23	        if self.null_unique_point(table, index, key) { return false; }
    24	        self.created.contains_key(&(table.to_owned(), index.to_owned(), crate::value::canonical_json(&key)))
    25	    }

    27	    /// A point read: the row when it exists and the viewer may read it, else
    28	    /// `null`. Hidden and absent are the same word on purpose.
    29	    pub(super) fn get(&mut self, read: &Read) -> Result<Value, RuntimeError> {
    30	        if self.decoration_cache.is_some() { return self.decoration_get(read); }
    31	        let value = self.get_uncached(read)?;
    32	        #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    33	        if self.following_witnesses.is_some() && let Value::Row(fields) = &value {
    34	            let bytes = 256 + read.table.len() as u64 + fields.keys().map(|f| f.len() as u64 + 32).sum::<u64>() + value.field("id")?.as_str()?.len() as u64;
    35	            self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
    36	            self.following_witnesses.as_mut().unwrap().push(super::following_history::projection::Witness { table:read.table.clone(),id:value.field("id")?.as_str()?.into(),fields:fields.keys().cloned().collect() });
    37	        }
    38	        Ok(value)
    39	    }

    41	    pub(super) fn get_uncached(&mut self, read: &Read) -> Result<Value, RuntimeError> {
    42	        let expiry = self.next_expiry.scope();
    43	        let mut emitted = false;
    44	        self.schema.refuse_private(&read.table)?;
    45	        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.21 — an unfinished maintained value is unavailable, never an absent group coerced to zero.
    46	        let maintained = self.schema.maintain_for(&read.table).is_some();
    47	        if maintained { self.meter.require_uncapped()?; }
    48	        let mut value = self.get_inner(read, &mut emitted)?;
    49	        if maintained { self.meter.require_uncapped()?; }
    50	        if emitted && self.meter.capped_at.is_none() { self.stamp_source(&read.table, &mut value)?; expiry.emit(); }
    51	        Ok(value)
    52	    }
    53	
    54	    fn get_inner(&mut self, read: &Read, emitted: &mut bool) -> Result<Value, RuntimeError> {
    55	        let key = read.key.iter().map(|value| self.expr(value)).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
    56	        if self.null_unique_point(&read.table, &read.index, &key) { return Ok(Value::Null); }
    57	        self.observe_sequence_selection(&read.table, &read.index, &key)?;
    58	        let table = self.schema.table(&read.table).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {}", read.table)))?;
    59	        self.read_tables.insert(read.table.clone());
    60	        self.rule_dependencies(&table.rules.read);
    61	        self.meter.at(&read.site);
    62	        self.aggregate_read_coverage(&read.table, &read.index, &key, &read.site)?;
    63	        let Some(maintain) = self.schema.maintain_for(&read.table) else {
    64	            let (value, price) = self.get_prepared(read, &key, emitted)?;
    65	            self.meter.heap(price)?;
    66	            return Ok(value);
    67	        };
    68	        // @ref LLP 3000.028#3.4 — a generation-wide acquired flag cannot lend another caller an empty owner partition.
    69	        if self.device && maintain.own_keys.is_some() && !self.tx.current_group(&read.table, &read.index, &key)? {
    70	            self.unknown_fact(&read.table, &read.index, &key, &read.site);
    71	            self.components.note(|frame| frame.speculative = true);
    72	            return Ok(Value::Null);
    73	        }
    74	        if let Some(message) = maintain.expiring_read_refusal(self.schema) {
    75	            return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_MAINTAIN_READ_EXPIRE", message });
    76	        }
    77	        // @ref LLP 3000.014#5-what-derives-from-the-capture — a point hit, miss or denial reserves the same reusable row scratch before discovering occupancy.
    78	        let scratch = self.aggregate_point_scratch(maintain, &key);
    79	        self.meter.heap(scratch)?;
    80	        let result = (|| {
    81	            self.read_charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
    82	            self.meter.require_uncapped()?;
    83	            self.get_prepared(read, &key, emitted)
    84	        })();
    85	        // Transfer only the sealed result to retained ownership. Keep the
    86	        // high-water mark, work counters and any cut when releasing scratch.
    87	        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = self.meter.used.heap_bytes.saturating_sub(scratch);
    88	        let (value, price) = result?;
    89	        self.meter.heap(price)?;
    90	        Ok(value)
    91	    }

    93	    /// The answer and the sealed price of its retained image, charged by the caller
    94	    /// once its scratch is released.
    95	    fn get_prepared(&mut self, read: &Read, key: &[Value], emitted: &mut bool) -> Result<(Value, u64), RuntimeError> {
    96	        let table = self.schema.table(&read.table).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {}", read.table)))?;
    97	        let index = table.index(&read.index).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing index {}.{}", read.table, read.index)))?;
    98	        let maintained = self.schema.maintain_for(&read.table);
    99	        let inherited = maintained.filter(|m| self.schema.tables[&m.source].through.is_some());
   100	        let mut key_admitted = false;
   101	        // @ref LLP 3000.014#5-what-derives-from-the-capture — only key-determined inputs may authorize a synthetic aggregate row.
   102	        if let Some(m) = inherited.filter(|m| m.parent_key.is_some() || rules::deciding_fields(&read.table, table, &table.rules.read).iter().all(|field| index.columns().iter().take(key.len()).any(|column| column == field) || (field == "id" && m.group_fields().iter().all(|f| index.columns().iter().take(key.len()).any(|column| column == f))))) {
   103	            let visible = (|| Ok(if let Some(parent) = &m.parent_key {
   104	                let Some(at) = index.columns().iter().position(|f| f == &parent.reference) else { return Err(RuntimeError::Structural {code:"E_READ_THROUGH_SCAN",message:format!("{} must be read by its full parent key; use {}[parent] (guide maintains)",read.table,read.table)}); };
   105	                let parent_id = key.get(at).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("read through aggregate needs its full parent key".into()))?;
   106	                match self.parent_verdict(&m.source,parent,parent_id)? {
   107	                    super::through::ParentVerdict::Readable => true,
   108	                    super::through::ParentVerdict::Unknown => { self.unknown_fact(&read.table,&read.index,key,&read.site); false },
   109	                    _ => false,
   110	                }
   111	            } else {
   112	                let mut fields: BTreeMap<_, _> = crate::small_map::collect(index.columns().into_iter().zip(key.iter().cloned()));
   113	                let group_fields = m.group_fields();
   114	                if group_fields.iter().all(|f| fields.contains_key(f)) {
   115	                    let group: Vec<_> = group_fields.iter().map(|f| fields[f].clone()).collect();
   116	                    fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(crate::schema::maintained_id(&group)));
   117	                }
   118	                let row = Value::Row(fields.into());

   120	                let viewer = self.context.viewer.clone();

   125	                    // witnesses still run under the request's physical allowance and

   128	                }

   133	                self.unknown_fact(&read.table, &read.index, key, &read.site);
   134	                return Ok((unavailable_aggregate(), 0));
   135	            }
   136	            if self.device && m.parent_key.is_some() {
   137	                // A locally synthesized total has no settled row to freeze.
   138	                // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — never recount provisional receipt inputs.

   140	                if self.beyond_horizon || self.receipt_maintain_pending(m, group.as_deref())? { return Ok((unavailable_aggregate(), 0)); }

   142	                // its generated table need not have an invertible sync audience.

   149	                return Ok((sealed.into_value(), price));
   150	            }
   151	        }

   157	        }

   169	        // missing aggregate before its logical zero is disclosed. A hidden hit

   174	        let found = self.authorized_point(read, index, key, prepaid, trusted, maintained.is_some(), &mut absent)?;

   203	                return Ok((Value::Null, 0));
   204	            }
   205	            self.read_tables = tables_mark;
   206	            return Ok((if maintained.is_some() { unavailable_aggregate() } else { Value::Null }, 0));
   207	        };
   208	        let price = row.heap_bytes() + row.projection_heap() + row.materialization_heap();
   209	        let mut value = row.into_value();
   210	        // @ref LLP 3000.014#5 — retained history stays marked through projections; ordinary retained
   211	        // point reads keep their established component composition (the row-level fallback is read-through's).
   212	        if self.device && table.through.is_some() && self.context.row_provenance && self.retained_row(&read.table, &value)? {
   213	            if let Value::Row(fields) = &mut value { fields.mark_retained(); }
   214	        }
   215	        let value = self.sequence_read_result(&read.table, value)?;
   216	        *emitted = true;
   217	        Ok((if matches!(self.timeline_authority, Some(super::timeline_authority::Authority::Transition(_))) { value }

   220	}

    12	    pub(super) fn aggregate_point_scratch(&self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> u64 {

    27	            })

    30	    /// A maintain over expiring source rows is a live fact before the

    40	            return Ok(Some(row));
    41	        };

    43	        if maintain.row_key.is_some() { return self.live_row_view(maintain, row); }

    56	                    .saturating_mul(16),

   438	    fn join_loop_binding(&self, local: &str, old: &mut Binding, new: &Binding, site: &Site) -> Fallible<(bool, bool)> {
   439	        debug_assert_eq!(new.runtime, old.runtime);

   195	        Expr::Name { name, .. } => matches!(name.as_str(), "now" | "viewer") || required.contains(name),
   196	        Expr::Unary { .. } | Expr::Binary { .. } => numeric_interval(value, required).is_some(),
   197	        _ => false,
   198	    }
   199	}

   201	
   202	fn numeric_interval(value: &Expr, required: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<(i128, i128)> {
   203	    let max = i128::from(snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX);
   204	    let (low, high) = match value {
   205	        Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Number(number), .. } => { let n = number.parse().ok()?; (n, n) }
   206	        Expr::Name { .. } if safe_endpoint(value, required) => (-max, max),
   207	        Expr::Unary { op, value, .. } if op == "-" => { let (lo, hi) = numeric_interval(value, required)?; (-hi, -lo) }
   208	        Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. } => {
   209	            let (a, b) = numeric_interval(left, required)?;
   210	            let (c, d) = numeric_interval(right, required)?;
   211	            match op.as_str() {
   212	                "+" => (a + c, b + d),
   213	                "-" => (a - d, b - c),
   214	                "*" => { let products = [a * c, a * d, b * c, b * d]; (*products.iter().min()?, *products.iter().max()?) }
   215	                _ => return None,
   216	            }
   217	        }
   218	        _ => return None,
   219	    };
   220	    (low >= -max && high <= max).then_some((low, high))
   221	}

   246	fn baseline_page_call<S: snapback4_device::store::DeviceStore>(device: &mut Device<S>, request: Json) -> Json {
   247	    use snapback4_core::error::RuntimeError;
   248	    let result = (|| {
   249	        let op = request.get("op").and_then(Json::as_str).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("the call needs op".into()))?;
   250	        if !matches!(op, "apply" | "observe_store") { return Err(RuntimeError::UnknownOp(op.into())); }
   251	        let value = request.get("page").ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("the call needs page".into()))?;
   252	        let page: StreamPage = serde_json::from_value(value.clone()).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Input(e.to_string()))?;
   253	        if op == "observe_store" { return Ok(serde_json::to_value(device.observe_store(&page)?).unwrap()); }
   254	        let touched = device.apply(&page, request.get("first").and_then(Json::as_bool).unwrap_or(false))?;
   255	        Ok(json!({ "touched": touched, "published": !device.publication_pending()? }))
   256	    })();
   257	    match result { Ok(value) => json!({"ok":value}), Err(error) => json!({"denied": serde_json::to_value(error.refusal()).unwrap()}) }
   258	}

   165	#[test]
   166	fn the_monthly_billing_recipe_catches_up_once() {

   168	    let card = snapback4_lang::guide::card("time").unwrap();
   169	    let block = snapback4_lang::guide::quarry(card).into_iter().find(|b| b.contains("job bill(")).unwrap();
   170	    let b = clean(&block);

   173	    let month = |m: i64| snapback4_core::calendar::month_start(m).unwrap();
   174	    let nine = 9 * 3_600_000;
   175	    let at = |m: i64| month(m) + nine; // 09:00 on the 1st of month ordinal m
   176	    let oct = 681;
   177	    let sent = |o: snapback4_core::MutationOutcome| matches!(o.state, snapback4_core::WriteState::Sent { .. });
   178	    assert!(sent(e.mutate("subscribe", None, Context::new("alice", [("plan".to_owned(), Value::Id("pro".into()))].into()).at(month(oct) + 10 * 86_400_000)).unwrap()));
   179	    let invoices = |e: &Engine| {
   180	        let mut months: Vec<i64> = e.store().rows("invoices").unwrap().iter().map(|r| r.field("month").unwrap().as_int().unwrap()).collect();
   181	        months.sort();
   182	        months
   183	    };
   184	    let mut fire = |e: &mut Engine, now: i64| {
   185	        let fired = e.fire_schedules(now).unwrap();
   186	        while let Some(run) = e.run_job_chunk(now).unwrap() {
   187	            assert_eq!(run.state, snapback4_core::JobState::Done, "{run:?}");
   188	        }
   189	        fired
   190	    };
   191	    assert!(fire(&mut e, at(oct)).is_empty(), "a schedule first seen fires from its next boundary");
   192	    assert_eq!(fire(&mut e, at(oct + 1)), ["billing"]);
   193	    assert_eq!(invoices(&e), [oct]);
   194	    // Down through December and January: one coalesced run on February 1st bills both, once.
   195	    assert_eq!(fire(&mut e, at(oct + 4)), ["billing"]);
   196	    assert_eq!(invoices(&e), [oct, oct + 1, oct + 2, oct + 3]);
   197	    assert!(fire(&mut e, at(oct + 4) + 1).is_empty());

   208	    e.seed([("subscriptions".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("old".into())), ("owner", Value::Id("bob".into())), ("plan", Value::Id("pro".into())), ("startMonth", Value::Int(oct - 30)), ("billedThrough", Value::Int(oct - 31))]))]).unwrap();

    37	        let constraints = wire["tables"][backend.schema.tables.keys().next().unwrap()]["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap();
    38	        let at = constraints.iter().position(|c| c.get("Capabilities").is_some()).unwrap();
    39	        match mode {
    40	            "missing-timeline" => constraints[at] = json!({"Capabilities":["recorded-attribution"]}),
    41	            "missing-recorded" => constraints[at] = json!({"Capabilities":["timeline"]}),
    42	            "unknown" => constraints[at] = json!({"Capabilities":["recorded-attribution", "timeline", "future-derivation"]}),
    43	            "duplicate" => constraints.push(constraints[at].clone()),
    44	            "missing" => { constraints.remove(at); }

    21	// @ref LLP 3000.013#2.1 — intrinsic id resolves every table-local tie.
    22	// Normalize authored table reads before view expansion: a view's shared order
    23	// must retain later keys because different branches can carry the same id.
    24	pub(super) fn table_order(catalog: &mut Catalog) {
    25	    let mut normalize = |value: &mut Expr| {
    26	        if let Expr::Read(read) = value && read.matching.is_some() && read.index.is_some()
    27	            && let Some(table) = catalog.tables.get(&read.table) {
    28	            let original = read.clone();
    29	            if super::intent_search::named_order(table, read) {
    30	                let source = catalog.source.expression(&Expr::Read(original));
    31	                catalog.read_origins.entry(read.site.to_string()).or_insert_with(|| source.clone());
    32	                catalog.canonical_read_origins.entry(read.site.to_string()).or_insert(source);
    33	            }
    34	        }
    35	        if let Expr::Read(read) | Expr::Exists { read, .. } = value
    36	            && catalog.tables.contains_key(&read.table)
    37	            && let Some(id) = read.order_keys.iter().position(|column| column == "id")
    38	            && id + 1 < read.order_keys.len() {
    39	            catalog.read_origins.entry(read.site.to_string()).or_insert_with(|| catalog.source.expression(&Expr::Read(read.clone())));
    40	            catalog.canonical_read_origins.entry(read.site.to_string()).or_insert_with(|| if read.index.is_none() { crate::print::read_expr(read) } else { catalog.source.expression(&Expr::Read(read.clone())) });
    41	            read.order_keys.truncate(id + 1);
    42	        }
    43	    };
    44	    for doc in &mut catalog.documents {
    45	        walk::document(doc, &mut normalize);
    46	        for view in &mut doc.views {
    47	            for branch in &mut view.branches {
    48	                if let Some(predicate) = &mut branch.predicate { walk::expression(predicate, &mut normalize); }
    49	                walk::shape(&mut branch.fields, &mut normalize);
    50	            }
    51	        }
    52	    }
    53	}

   285	                rusqlite::params![n.to_string(), payload]).unwrap();

   288	            INSERT INTO _meta VALUES ('device:declaration:capture','{}');
   289	            INSERT OR REPLACE INTO _meta VALUES ('device:send_revision','9007199254740991'); COMMIT;
   290	            CREATE TABLE free_page_fixture(data BLOB);
   291	            INSERT INTO free_page_fixture VALUES (zeroblob(4194304));
   292	            DROP TABLE free_page_fixture;").unwrap();
   293	        drop(db); // Checkpoint the large fixture before retaining a small WAL.
   294	        if mode == "WAL" {
   295	            let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(&path).unwrap();
   296	            db.set_db_config(rusqlite::config::DbConfig::SQLITE_DBCONFIG_NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE, true).unwrap();
   297	            db.execute_batch("PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0; INSERT INTO _meta VALUES ('sg:sentinel','retained committed WAL');").unwrap();
   298	        }

   300	        let bytes = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
   301	        let wal_path = std::path::PathBuf::from(format!("{}-wal", path.display()));
   302	        let wal = std::fs::read(&wal_path).ok();
   303	        let error = snapback4_device::native::Device::open(&path, None).err().expect("late recovery refusal");
   304	        assert!(error.to_string().contains("send revision overflow"), "{error}");
   305	        let after_bytes = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
   306	        assert_eq!(after_bytes.len(), bytes.len());

   323	            assert!(after.starts_with(&wal), "committed uncheckpointed frames survive; only uncommitted frames are appended");

   342	fn freelist_leaves(bytes: &[u8]) -> std::collections::BTreeSet<u32> {
   343	    let word = |offset| u32::from_be_bytes(bytes[offset..offset + 4].try_into().unwrap());
   344	    let size = u16::from_be_bytes([bytes[16], bytes[17]]) as usize;
   345	    let mut trunk = word(32);
   346	    let mut leaves = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
   347	    while trunk != 0 {
   348	        let offset = (trunk as usize - 1) * size;
   349	        for n in 0..word(offset + 4) as usize { assert!(leaves.insert(word(offset + 8 + n * 4))); }
   350	        trunk = word(offset);
   351	    }
   352	    leaves
   353	}

   362	fn group_keys(maintain: &ast::MaintainDecl, read: &ReadExpr) -> BTreeMap<String, A> {
   363	    if maintain.by.len() != read.keys.len() { return BTreeMap::new(); }

   372	/// Rule constants occupy their own namespace. Freeze that identity before a

   375	pub(in crate::bind) fn normalize_rule_constants(expression: &mut A) {

   125	Finance reads every department's total; each requester reads their own.
   126	`E_QUARRY_BOUND`'s rewrite prints this view for your table, column and group.
   127	A keyed private view stays nullable until its own read rule is proved. For
   128	example, after `require exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance']
   129	else NOT_FINANCE`, `requestsTotal[dept] + 1` is well typed and a readable
   130	missing group contributes zero. A hidden stored group and a hidden miss both
   131	remain null. A following write or viewer change invalidates the proof before
   132	another keyed read.
   133	A view may omit `by` for a whole-table scalar: `view requestsCount: count
   134	requests`, read as bare `requestsCount`. The scalar still obeys its view read
   135	rule: an authorized absence is zero, while a hidden stored or absent value is
   136	null. Keep a real group key when callers need independent totals.
   137	A guard on the read rule's own grant admits an inline total, as it admits a
   138	staff page (`guide indexes`): after `require exists staff[principal = viewer,
   139	role = 'finance'] else …` (or inside `if` on it), `sum(requests, .amount)` is
   140	every row's total, because every caller who reaches it reads every row. A guard
   141	on any other role does not; use the view.
   142	
   143	For extrema over a domain, first establish that exact domain is non-empty:
   144	`n = count(orders where .owner = viewer)` followed by `require n > 0 else
   145	EMPTY`. From there, `min` and `max` of a required column on the identical
   146	domain are required values; `sum` already has a zero identity. Optional projected columns remain optional. A
   147	write, local rebinding, viewer/authority scope change, or different key/filter
   148	invalidates the proof.
   149	
   150	## Choosing
   151	
   152	- A total a screen shows on every visit: a view. It is maintained on each
   153	  write and read by key, constant work regardless of history.
   154	- A rolling window (last 7 days): bucket the view by `day(.at)` (or
   155	  `hour(.at)`, `bucket(.at, 15m)`) and add the buckets you need with point
   156	  reads, `perDay[viewer, day(now)] + perDay[viewer, day(now) - 1]`.
   157	- A one-off or filtered total (since an argument, by status): `count(...)` or
   158	  `sum(...)` in the operation. It streams the domain under the meter: each
   159	  row is authorized, filtered, folded and released. Its work grows with the
   160	  matching rows, and `check --cost` says so; bound the predicate by an indexed
   161	  time or a group key.
   162	- `count(page)` and `sum(page, .col)` over a page you already read count only
   163	  that page, not the population.
   164	
   165	## Details
   166	
   167	A meter cut never yields a partial total: the read is unavailable (the client
   168	shows `loading`), including before `??`. On a device, an inline total needs
   169	the device to hold its whole domain; otherwise the observation stays
   170	`loading`, never a partial total. Sums take `int`, `decimal` or `money` columns; a total
   171	that overflows refuses the transaction. `guide maintains` has every view form
   172	(filters, reference paths, time buckets, offsets and sync); `guide reads`
   173	covers totals beside pages and `exists`; `guide jobs` the sweep a job's totals
   174	live in.
   175	
   176	Common misspellings and what `check` says:
   177	
   178	- `sum(orders of .cents)` (the view spelling inside an operation):
   179	  `E_QUARRY_UNKNOWN: unknown shape of`. Write `sum(orders where …, .cents)`.
   180	- `count orders where .owner = viewer` without parentheses:
   181	  `E_QUARRY_UNKNOWN: unknown shape where`. Write `count(orders where …)`.
   182	- `sum(orders where …, cents)`: `E_QUARRY_UNKNOWN: unknown name cents`. The
   183	  column is `.cents`.
   184	
   185	Reference-grouped views over `read through .parent` rows inherit the parent's
   186	rule. Omit a read line that repeats `.parent.owner = viewer`; it is
   187	`E_REDUNDANT_RULE`, and deleting the whole line preserves the inherited audience.
   188	Maintained sums spell the value separately: `view total: sum expenses of .amount by .household`,
   189	not `sum expenses.amount by .household`.

     1	//! The engine against the Lean model (LLP 3000.035 §5.2).
     2	//!
     3	//! **The model side.** Each case's surface program goes through
     4	//! `snapback4_lang::emit::lean` (the parsed tree, never the binder's IR) to
     5	//! the model's case JSON, and through `quarry-oracle` (`snapback4/lean`,
     6	//! `lake build`), one long-lived process per worker that answers one tagged
     7	//! outcome per line. A case the emitter cannot translate is `Unsupported`
     8	//! under the emitter's named reason, never a pass.
     9	//!
    10	//! **The engine side.** The engine over SQLite (the ordinary in-memory
    11	//! server store) at `Ceilings::default()`, the ceilings a production server
    12	//! runs, not the case's stored budget; the model runs unbounded (its meter is
    13	//! abstract, OPEN M1).
    14	//!
    15	//! **Compared fields** (README, "How the harness compares"):
    16	//!
    17	//! - `kind`: answer, unavailable, refused, committed;
    18	//! - `code`: the refusal code (sites are not modelled);
    19	//! - `data` / `result`: exact, both sides as tagged values, so an id never
    20	//!   compares equal to a text (OPEN V1); rows compare as field maps;
    21	//! - `complete`: exact;
    22	//! - `next`: presence only (OPEN C1). When both carry one, each side
    23	//!   continues from its own cursor and the next page is compared
    24	//!   (`continuation-*`), until both are exhausted;
    25	//! - a mutation then runs `observe` on each side's resulting store
    26	//!   (`post-*`): the engine's store, and the model's committed store (or the
    27	//!   original store after a refusal).
    28	//!
    29	//! Meter fields, cut sites, `tables` and `seq` are not compared. Expiry
    30	//! sweeps advance both stores before the following program is compared.
    31	//!
    32	//! **Signatures** are `lean--{field}--{engine}~{model}`, each side's stable
    33	//! class (a refusal code, `unavailable`, `committed`, or the data's shape).
    34	//! The finding's `left` is the engine's raw record, `right` the model's raw
    35	//! outcome; the canonical forms compared are its `continuation`.

    56	/// The `quarry-oracle` executable: `SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE`, else the Lake

    58	pub fn oracle_path() -> PathBuf {

    60	        Some(p) => PathBuf::from(p),

    65	/// Bring this checkout's `quarry-oracle` up to date with its model sources
    66	/// (`lake build quarry-oracle`, under a second when current). A merge or
    67	/// checkout that changes `lean/` leaves the previous executable in `.lake`,
    68	/// and the harness would report that older model's choices as disagreements
    69	/// (2026-10-12: a stale pre-guard oracle on the merged `sb4-loop` tree showed
    70	/// `lean--complete--complete~incomplete`). Nothing is done when
    71	/// `SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE` names the oracle (the caller vouches for it; a
    72	/// campaign's workers inherit the refreshed path that way) or when `lake` is
    73	/// not installed (a missing oracle still refuses at `LeanProcess::spawn`).
    74	pub fn refresh() -> Result<(), String> {
    75	    if std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE").is_some() {
    76	        return Ok(());
    77	    }
    78	    let dir = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../lean");
    79	    // Keep the optional-tool path read-only, including a checkout whose model
    80	    // directory is not writable. A version probe writes no Lake build artifacts.
    81	    match Command::new("lake").arg("--version").current_dir(&dir).stdin(Stdio::null()).output() {
    82	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
    83	            eprintln!("lake not found: using the Lean oracle as built at {}", oracle_path().display());
    84	            return Ok(());
    85	        }
    86	        Err(e) => return Err(format!("lake: {e}")),
    87	        Ok(_) => {} // The build below reports actual toolchain/configuration errors.
    88	    }
    89	    // @ref LLP 3000.035#52-stage-2-a-small-lean-core — concurrent refreshes must not write the same Lake artifacts.
    90	    let cache = dir.join(".lake");
    91	    fs::create_dir_all(&cache).map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh cache: {e}"))?;
    92	    let refresh_lock = OpenOptions::new().create(true).truncate(false).read(true).write(true)
    93	        .open(cache.join("snapback4-refresh.lock")).map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh lock: {e}"))?;
    94	    refresh_lock.lock().map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh lock: {e}"))?;
    95	    match Command::new("lake").args(["build", "quarry-oracle"]).current_dir(&dir).stdin(Stdio::null()).output() {

    97	        Ok(output) => Err(format!(

   107	        Err(e) => Err(format!("lake: {e}")),
   108	    }

   111	/// One `quarry-oracle` process: a JSON case per line in, an outcome per line out.
   112	pub struct LeanProcess {
   113	    child: Child,
   114	    stdin: ChildStdin,
   115	    stdout: BufReader<ChildStdout>,
   116	}
   117	impl LeanProcess {
   118	    pub fn spawn() -> Result<Self, String> {
   119	        let path = oracle_path();
   120	        if !path.is_file() {
   121	            return Err(format!(
   122	                "Lean oracle missing: {} (run `cd snapback4/lean && lake build`, or set SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE)",
   123	                path.display()
   124	            ));
   125	        }
   126	        let mut child = Command::new(&path)
   127	            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
   128	            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
   129	            .stderr(Stdio::inherit())
   130	            .spawn()
   131	            .map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
   132	        let stdin = child.stdin.take().unwrap();
   133	        let stdout = BufReader::new(child.stdout.take().unwrap());
   134	        Ok(Self { child, stdin, stdout })
   135	    }
   136	    pub fn ask(&mut self, case: &Json) -> Result<Json, String> {
   137	        writeln!(self.stdin, "{case}").map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle write: {e}"))?;
   138	        self.stdin.flush().map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle flush: {e}"))?;
   139	        let mut line = String::new();
   140	        let n = self.stdout.read_line(&mut line).map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle read: {e}"))?;
   141	        if n == 0 {
   142	            return Err("Lean oracle exited".into());
   143	        }
   144	        let answer: Json = serde_json::from_str(&line).map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle answer {line:?}: {e}"))?;
   145	        if answer["kind"] == "error" {
   146	            // A case the model cannot decode is an emitter defect, never a verdict.
   147	            return Err(format!("Lean oracle refused the case: {}", answer["error"]));
   148	        }
   149	        Ok(answer)
   150	    }
   151	}
   152	impl Drop for LeanProcess {
   153	    fn drop(&mut self) {
   154	        let _ = self.child.kill();
   155	        let _ = self.child.wait();
   156	    }
   157	}
   158	
   159	thread_local! {
   160	    static PROCESS: RefCell<Option<LeanProcess>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };
   161	}
   162	
   163	/// Ask this thread's oracle process, starting it on first use and once
   164	/// more if it has died.
   165	pub fn ask(case: &Json) -> Result<Json, String> {
   166	    PROCESS.with(|cell| {
   167	        let mut slot = cell.borrow_mut();
   168	        if slot.is_none() {
   169	            *slot = Some(LeanProcess::spawn()?);
   170	        }
   171	        match slot.as_mut().unwrap().ask(case) {
   172	            Err(e) if e == "Lean oracle exited" => {
   173	                *slot = Some(LeanProcess::spawn()?);
   174	                slot.as_mut().unwrap().ask(case)
   175	            }
   176	            other => other,
   177	        }
   178	    })
   179	}

- **P2 — Expression extrema still bypass the global scalar boundary.** For a public `view total: count entries`, `min((total where true by byId), .value + 0)` and the equivalent `max` can scan physical aggregate rows instead of refusing. `aggregate_domain` excludes globals, but the fallback registry still records them (`dcd85ffa57:snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/intent_aggregates.rs:64`). `extremum` retrieves that domain, discards the global-read diagnostic, and calls `scan_at` (`dcd85ffa57:snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/program/extrema.rs:11`, `:23`, `:41`). This leaves prior counterexample 1 incompletely closed. Reject ungrouped targets on this fallback or at the shared scan boundary, with expression-valued `min`/`max` regressions.
